note_title: Two empty arms, one listening God.
note_body: Abram asks his ache out loud; Hannah weeps hers at Shiloh's doorpost. Neither dresses up the sorrow, and neither is turned away — honest longing is a language heaven understands.
lens_gloss: stripped, childless — the bare word Abram hands to God, naming the ache without dressing it up.

note_title: The sea remembers, and so does He.
note_body: Moses sings of chariots swallowed once; generations later Isaiah still names God as the One who brings out horse and army only to lay them down, never to rise. What outmatched Pharaoh's confidence was no one-time wonder — it is His settled way with whatever oppresses His own.
lens_gloss: to hurl, to cast — one decisive throw of the Lord's arm, flinging oppression's whole arsenal into the deep.

note_title: Not one foot of ground, yet promised.
note_body: God names Canaan an everlasting possession while Abraham is still a stranger in it; Stephen remembers that Abraham owned not so much as a footprint's worth. The promise was true the whole in-between time — and so was the belonging.
lens_gloss: sojournings, temporary lodgings — God speaks 'everlasting' directly over the address that still feels temporary.

note_body: Israel was brought out of bondage 'because the LORD loved you' — before land, strength, or a finished testimony. Paul says the same of us: rich mercy and great love came while there was nothing in our hands to show.
lens_gloss: love — named as the only reason for redemption; covenant affection that moves before any performance exists.

note_title: Two ways to hear 'go thy way.'
note_body: Pharaoh's 'go thy way' carries the sting of truth exposed; the Preacher's 'go thy way' carries bread, wine, and acceptance. Correction walks you out the door, and grace meets you on the road with a table.
lens_gloss: go! — the command that first launched Abram in Genesis 12:1 returns through correction, still pointed toward the promise.

note_body: Genesis opens with God creating; John opens with the same three words and shows us the Word who was already there. Before anything was asked of you, everything was held by Him.
lens_gloss: in the beginning — before demands, measurements, or unfinished lists, God already was; John opens with the same doorway.

note_title: Two shepherds, called from the sheepfolds.
note_body: Moses is keeping Jethro's flock when he comes upon the mountain of God; David is minding sheep when God reaches into the fold and chooses him. Ordinary faithfulness is not delay — it is where callings learn to walk.
lens_gloss: shepherding, tending — the ordinary working verb Moses was living inside when he arrived at the mountain of God.

note_title: Folds for the sheep, then forward.
note_body: Joseph leaves the little ones and flocks safe in Goshen before the hard journey; the tribes build cities for their children and folds for their sheep before crossing over to the fight. Love settles what is tender into safety so obedience can travel light.
lens_gloss: little ones, the toddling dependents — what is most vulnerable gets settled in safety, not hauled onto the hard road.

note_title: The nourisher of old age, twice.
note_body: The women bless Naomi with a restorer of life and a nourisher of her old age; Isaiah hears God claim that very office — 'even to hoar hairs will I carry you.' When Ruth's love carried Naomi, it was showing the neighborhood what God's arms look like.
lens_gloss: restorer of the soul — Psalm 23's 'he restoreth my soul,' here wearing the arms of a devoted family.

note_title: A staff, a throne, same posture.
note_body: Jacob remembers crossing the Jordan with nothing but a staff; David sits before the LORD asking who am I, that thou hast brought me hitherto. Both men count their increase and call it mercy, not merit.
lens_gloss: 'I have become small' — Jacob's whole prayer in one verb, shrinking gladly beneath mercies too many to earn.

note_body: At the mountain God names Israel a kingdom of priests and a holy nation; Peter takes those very words and lays them on ordinary believers. The identity came before anyone knew how to carry it — both times.
lens_gloss: priests — a whole people granted holy access and holy errand; identity conferred before anyone knew how to carry it.

note_title: The lifted face Jacob longed for.
note_body: Jacob sends gifts ahead hoping Esau will 'accept' him — in Hebrew, lift his face. In Job, God uses the same idiom and simply gives it: 'him will I accept.' What we scheme to earn from people, the Father grants freely.
lens_gloss: to cover, to appease — the root of Yom Kippur hiding in Jacob's plan; the welcome he schemes for, God gives freely.

note_title: Herein is love: He started it.
note_body: Deuteronomy says plainly that Israel's smallness was no obstacle, because the choosing began in God's heart, not their headcount. John closes the circle: herein is love — not that we loved Him, but that He loved us.
lens_gloss: to be bound to in love, to cling — affection that fastens itself to the small and never checks the measurements.

note_body: In Eden the food is given before a single field is worked; Jesus points to birds who never sow or reap, yet eat from the Father's hand. Provision has always come from grace before it ever came from performance.
lens_gloss: to give — creation's first economy is gift; the table stands set before anyone has earned a single meal.

note_body: Joseph, whose road ran through betrayal and prison, holds Machir's children on his knees; Job, whose road ran through ashes, sees his sons' sons to the fourth generation. God writes futures long enough to outlive the worst chapter.
lens_gloss: third-generation children — hope measured three lifetimes deep, held on the knees of a man grief could not finish.

note_title: Purchased at the sea and the cross.
note_body: Israel passes through dread because they are a people God 'purchased'; Titus says Jesus gave Himself to redeem a peculiar people for His own possession. You move forward not because fear is gone, but because you are bought and belonged.
lens_gloss: to purchase, acquire as one's own — the people pass through dread because they are owned by love, not powered by courage.

note_title: Made in His image, His workmanship.
note_body: Genesis says God created humankind in His own image; Paul says we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus. Twice-made and twice-claimed — your worth was authored, not invented.
lens_gloss: image — worth stamped into the making by the Maker Himself, never self-invented and never revoked.

note_body: David enters God's house 'in the multitude of thy mercy,' not in the strength of his record; Hebrews says come boldly to the throne — to obtain mercy. Both doors swing on the same hinge, and it was never our performance.
lens_gloss: steadfast covenant love — the abundance David walks in on; entrance to God's house was mercy's idea first.

note_body: Genesis shows humankind made in God's image before a single assignment is handed out; Colossians shows the new man 'renewed after the image of him that created him.' First He tells you who you are — then, and only then, what to do.
lens_gloss: likeness — humankind patterned on God before being put to work; resemblance comes before responsibility.

note_body: The news of Joseph's complicated family pleases Pharaoh's whole house; the church's aired grievance ends in a resolution that pleases the whole multitude. When God manages the telling, exposure meets grace instead of contempt.
lens_gloss: voice, sound, report — the long-hidden story finally becomes sound in the open, and mercy is what meets it.

note_body: Exodus binds mercy to those who love God and keep His commandments; John says that keeping them is what loving Him looks like — and they are not grievous. Holiness is not the opposite of love; it is love's shape.
lens_gloss: thousands — covenant mercy counted in generations upon generations; love with long arithmetic and a longer memory.

note_body: Moses calls Him the faithful God who keeps covenant and mercy to a thousand generations; Paul goes further still — if we believe not, He abides faithful, for He cannot deny Himself. His love has memory, and it does not have moods.
lens_gloss: firm, faithful — the root behind 'amen'; a love you can lean your whole weight on without it moving.

note_body: Joseph sends wagons and packs provision at Pharaoh's command; Josiah's Passover is prepared the same day, according to the commandment. In both houses, care is not a feeling floating somewhere — it is loaded, scheduled, and delivered.
lens_gloss: provision for the road — love that thinks ahead to the miles you must travel and packs accordingly.

note_title: Lamps hung by the Father of lights.
note_body: Genesis hangs lights in the heavens to give light on the earth — and it was so; James names God the Father of lights, from whom every good gift comes down. You do not manufacture your light; you receive it.
lens_gloss: light-bearer, lamp — the heavens hold lamps they did not light; every shining thing carries a light it was given.

note_body: Israel camps before the mountain with no instruction yet visible; Moses waited forty years in that same wilderness before the bush burned. God's pauses are not abandonment — they are positioning.
lens_gloss: to pitch camp — a stop that is not a stall; Israel parks its whole life in front of God on purpose.

note_body: Jacob's present crosses over while he lodges that night in camp; Joshua sends the ambush ahead and lodges that night among the people. Faith sometimes does the next right thing and then must simply sleep, leaving the outcome in God's watch.
lens_gloss: to lodge for the night — faith learns to sleep between the obedient step and the answer that has not yet come.

note_title: What to do with hard seeing.
note_body: Esau finally sees that his choices displeased his father — and reaches for another surface fix; Samuel sees a displeasing thing and carries it straight to the LORD in prayer. Clear sight is mercy's doorway, but only prayer walks through it.
lens_gloss: to see, to perceive — awareness arriving late is still mercy's doorway, if what is seen is carried to God.

note_body: Israel is told to love the stranger because they wore that name in Egypt; Jesus stops to honor 'this stranger,' the one leper who returned. The Father keeps drawing our eyes to the outsider — and calling that love.
lens_gloss: sojourner, resident outsider — the name Israel once wore in Egypt; remembered vulnerability becomes the engine of welcome.

note_title: A father's line, an apostle's echo.
note_body: Isaac draws a boundary around Jacob's future so the promise can breathe, and Paul draws the same line around the believer's heart. Some of God's no's are not punishment; they are a fence around what He is growing.
lens_gloss: to charge, command — a directive laid down in love, the way a father sets a guardrail around a promise

note_body: At the Red Sea the deep swallowed the army Israel could not outrun; in Micah the same depths receive our sins. The Redeemer drowns whatever pursues His children, even the pursuer inside.
lens_gloss: the deep — primeval waters no one can master, yet they obey the Redeemer and close over what chased His people

note_title: The wood on the son's back.
note_body: Isaac climbs Moriah carrying the wood for the offering; Jesus climbs Golgotha bearing His own cross. What Abraham's story could only whisper, the Father and the Son walked out in full, together.
lens_gloss: together, as one — father and son walking side by side into the hard place, neither one letting go

note_body: Genesis warns against despising the mark of belonging, and Paul warns against handling the covenant cup carelessly. In both testaments belonging to God is mercy taken seriously, a gift too holy to shrug at.
lens_gloss: to cut — the very verb Hebrew uses for making a covenant; refuse the covenant cut and you cut yourself off from it

note_body: At Sinai God comes in a thick cloud so the people can hear and believe; at the Transfiguration the cloud returns and the Voice says of the Son, 'hear ye him.' God has always drawn near to give faith something solid to stand on.
lens_gloss: cloud — the veil of Presence, thick enough to shield God's glory, near enough to carry His voice to trembling people

note_title: Not every open door is approval.
note_body: Abram's flocks multiply while Sarai sits unsafe in Pharaoh's house; Ecclesiastes asks what increase is really worth to its owner. Both texts teach the heart to examine a blessing before bowing to it.
lens_gloss: to do good, treat well — favor can flow from a troubled arrangement; kind treatment is not the same as God's approval

note_body: Moses says the LORD Himself is your life and the length of your days; Jesus stands at a tomb and says, 'I am the life.' The clinging Moses commanded finally found its face.
lens_gloss: to cling, hold fast, stay glued — love that stays attached to its Source instead of grasping for control

note_body: Genesis speaks an everlasting covenant whose heart is 'to be a God unto thee'; Hebrews hears the same voice writing that promise onto human hearts. The gift inside the covenant has always been God Himself.
lens_gloss: covenant — a binding bond of belonging in which God pledges not merely outcomes but His own presence

note_body: Genesis records the quiet moment Abram believed and righteousness was counted to him; James looks back and adds the title that trust earned, 'the Friend of God.' Believing before seeing is how friendship with the Father begins.
lens_gloss: to trust, lean firm — faith that rests its whole weight on the One who spoke, settled and sure

note_body: At Sinai God remembers bearing Israel on eagles' wings to Himself; in Revelation the wings are given again to carry His people to a nourished place. He has never stopped being the One who carries.
lens_gloss: to lift, bear, carry — grace hoists the whole people onto God's own strength before a single command is spoken

note_title: A token, a seal, a mercy.
note_body: Genesis gives the covenant a token to be carried in real life; Romans calls that same mark a seal of the righteousness of faith. God knows hearts forget under pressure, so He gives His promise somewhere to live.
lens_gloss: sign, token — a visible reminder set into daily life so a forgetful heart keeps finding the promise

note_body: Boaz has been told everything Ruth did and answers it with shelter and honor; David seeks out Mephibosheth to repay Jonathan's faithfulness at the king's own table. Costly love is never invisible to covenant kindness.
lens_gloss: to tell, declare — doubled in this verse, 'telling, it has been told me': not one detail of her faithfulness went unreported

note_body: Abraham trusts that God will see to the lamb, and keeps climbing; generations later John lifts his eyes and says, 'Behold the Lamb of God!' The provision was on its way before the question finished forming.
lens_gloss: to see — and therefore to see to it; God's providing is His looking ahead on your behalf before you arrive

note_body: Deuteronomy names the fear we count quietly inside, 'they are more than I'; Luke shows Jesus perceiving the thought of the heart and answering with gentleness instead of scorn. The Father meets the unspoken sum with Himself.
lens_gloss: heart — the inner chamber where fear speaks first; God answers what is said there before it is ever spoken aloud

note_body: A whole company of Egypt goes up with Joseph to bury his father; devout men carry Stephen to his grave with great lamentation. Scripture keeps showing that love does its heaviest lifting accompanied.
lens_gloss: to bury — love's last honoring duty, a weight the faithful in Scripture almost never carry alone

note_body: Israel sings at the water's edge that the LORD shall reign for ever and ever; heaven sings it again at the seventh trumpet, over every kingdom that thought it was permanent. The song was true at the shore, and it has not expired.
lens_gloss: to reign as king — confessed at the sea's edge, a rule that outlasts every pharaoh and every pressure

note_body: Isaac asks, 'where is the lamb?' and the question hangs over the whole story of Scripture until John points at Jesus: 'Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.' The Father let the question breathe until He could answer it in person.
lens_gloss: 'Here I am' — presence offered before explanation; a father's first gift to a questioning child is himself

note_body: Genesis sets the sign at eight days for every generation of the household; Luke shows Mary and Joseph keeping that very word with the infant Jesus. Faithfulness was handed down, hand to hand, until it cradled the Savior Himself.
lens_gloss: generation — faith is meant to travel; God gave the covenant legs to walk from parent to child

note_body: David's 'But I have trusted' and Habakkuk's 'Yet I will rejoice' are the same holy pivot: sorrow tells its whole truth, and then faith turns toward the God whose mercy never moved.
lens_gloss: steadfast, covenant-keeping love — mercy sturdy enough to hold a heart that is still walking out of anguish

note_body: Genesis names a set time for Isaac's arrival; Paul reaches back to that promise, 'at this time will I come, and Sara shall have a son,' to prove God's word has never failed. Heaven keeps a calendar, and it has never once run late.
lens_gloss: appointed time, a fixed meeting on God's calendar — your waiting has a date, even when you cannot read it

note_body: God tells Moses His name is His memorial to all generations; centuries later Jesus quotes that same introduction and adds, 'God of the living.' The name has not retired, and neither has the care behind it.
lens_gloss: remembrance, memorial — God binds His name to memory itself so no generation has to meet Him as a stranger

note_title: From one man, a night sky.
note_body: On Moriah God promises stars and sand to a man still trembling from obedience; Hebrews counts the multitude and marvels that it sprang from one 'as good as dead.' The promise outgrew the test that preceded it.
lens_gloss: to bless — doubled in the Hebrew, 'blessing I will bless thee': God's emphatic yes, wider than the day that tested you

note_body: The LORD tells Moses plainly that His people will drift toward rival gods; David gives Solomon the same sober charge: seek Him and be found. A holy welcome tells the truth about wandering because it intends to hold on to us.
lens_gloss: to forsake, abandon — the quiet walking-away that begins in the heart long before any idol is visible

note_body: God promises Abram covenant and exceeding increase, and Hebrews recalls the oath that later sealed it, 'multiplying I will multiply thee,' sworn so the heirs would have strong consolation. A promise repeated is meant to out-argue every expectation fear has shrunk.
lens_gloss: to multiply, make abundant — God's arithmetic for a future that fear had already rounded down

note_body: At Sinai God names His people His own treasure above all the earth; Peter hands the church the very same title, a peculiar people called out of darkness. Obedience is what treasured people do, not what unloved people attempt.
lens_gloss: a king's own treasured possession — not common inventory, but the treasure he keeps close and delights in

note_body: God cuts covenant with Abram and names actual rivers, giving trust real geography; Hebrews anchors our hope the same way, in the blood of an everlasting covenant and a risen Shepherd. God never asks a heart to rest on vapor.
lens_gloss: to give — spoken here as already accomplished: God signs the deed before the family ever holds the ground

note_body: Jacob is blessed with a land where he still lives as a sojourner; Hebrews says Abraham dwelt in that same promise as in a strange country. Faith stewards the tent while trusting the Father with the title.
lens_gloss: to sojourn, live as a resident stranger — heirs can dwell in tents a long while without losing the deed

note_title: Loved first, rescued because of it.
note_body: Deuteronomy says God brought Israel out because He loved their fathers; Jeremiah hears the same heart say, 'I have loved thee with an everlasting love.' Every rescue in your story started in an affection older than you.
lens_gloss: to love — the reason that stands before every rescue; God's choosing begins in affection, not obligation

note_body: Joseph keeps a sworn word and carries his father home to a prepared grave in Canaan; centuries later another Joseph gives his own hewn tomb to honor his Lord. Love that follows through does not stop at the graveside.
lens_gloss: to swear an oath — kin to the word for seven, a promise sealed as full and complete, binding the whole person.

note_title: A word laid down, a people standing.
note_body: Moses sets the Lord's words plainly before the elders' faces, and Paul sets the gospel plainly before Corinth — a word received, a word to stand in. In both houses, identity rests on what God has said, not on guesswork.
lens_gloss: word, matter, thing — in Hebrew a word carries substance and weight, speech solid enough to set a life upon.

note_body: Every man of Abraham's household carries the covenant sign together, and in Corinth Crispus believes on the Lord with all his house. God's promises keep drawing whole households into shared, dignified belonging.
lens_gloss: house, household — more than a building, the whole circle of lives carried under one roof and one covenant.

note_title: Known by name, held by grace.
note_body: Moses carries a calling too heavy for an anonymous servant, and he holds onto the word the Lord has already spoken — I know thee by name. The Good Shepherd says the same over His flock: being known comes before being sent.
lens_gloss: grace, favor — the warm tilt of God's face toward a servant, favor freely given before anything is earned.

note_title: The talk ends, the Word remains.
note_body: God finishes speaking and goes up from Abraham, and John says the Son in the Father's bosom has declared Him fully. Holy conversations close in God's own timing, but His self-revealing never stops.
lens_gloss: to go up, ascend — the unhurried close of a divine visit; God Himself ends the meeting in His own time.

note_title: A tree for the bitter water.
note_body: At Marah a God-shown tree turns bitterness sweet, and Paul says the preaching of the cross — foolishness to some — is the very power of God. Heaven still answers bitter places with a tree.
lens_gloss: to cry out — the loud, unpolished cry of someone in trouble; prayer before it learns to be tidy.

note_title: Only God walked the covenant path.
note_body: Jeremiah shows what passing between the pieces meant — the covenant-maker stakes his own life on his word. At Abram's altar God alone makes that passage, carrying the whole weight of the promise Himself.
lens_gloss: to pass through, cross over — here God alone makes the covenant crossing no human strength could make.

note_body: Moses promises that the Lord Himself will circumcise the heart until love becomes possible, and Paul says the true circumcision was always inward, of the spirit. God is not after polished behavior; He is after a freed heart.
lens_gloss: heart — the whole inner self, mind, will, and affection; the hidden place God's covenant surgery lovingly reaches.

note_title: Two families, two ways of seeing.
note_body: Esau watches a blessing he missed, and Miriam and Aaron speak against a brother over what they have taken in, letting it sour into complaint. What the eyes take in either ripens into honest conviction or curdles into resentment.
lens_gloss: to see, perceive — seeing that goes beyond the eyes; perception that can become conviction or harden into grievance.

note_body: Joseph tells the truth that five hard years remain, and Sinai commands rest even in plowing time and harvest. God paces His people honestly through seasons that will not end tomorrow.
lens_gloss: famine, hunger — the long ache of a land, a hardship Scripture names plainly without shrinking or dressing it up.

note_title: The Lord Himself meets the rising.
note_body: Israel sings of God overthrowing those who rose up against Him, and on the Damascus road it is Jesus Himself who stops Saul in his tracks. Deliverance was never our impressiveness; it is His doing.
lens_gloss: majesty, exaltation — the towering height of God's excellency that no rising enemy, and no anxious striving, can reach.

note_body: Jacob's heart goes numb at the word that Joseph lives, and the risen Jesus finds His friends believing not for joy. In both rooms mercy waits patiently while wonder catches up with the truth.
lens_gloss: to grow numb, go faint — the heart's stunned pause when news is too large to feel all at once.

note_title: Two handmaids, lifted by kind words.
note_body: Ruth says Boaz's friendly words comforted her heart, and Hannah leaves Shiloh with her face no longer sad after one gracious blessing. A kind sentence can send fear packing and let courage breathe again.
lens_gloss: to comfort, console — consolation strong enough to change the breathing, settling a fearful heart where it actually lives.

note_body: In Pharaoh's house the Lord steps in where Sarai has no other defender, and generations later the psalmist sings it plainly — He reproved kings for their sakes. What God interrupts, He is protecting.
lens_gloss: plague, stroke, blow — God's firm touch that exposes hidden harm and refuses to let it remain hidden.

note_title: Mercy deep enough to be just.
note_body: Sinai reveals a God who keeps mercy for thousands yet stays morally serious, and John says He is faithful and just to forgive what we honestly confess. Grace never has to pretend sin is small.
lens_gloss: steadfast covenant love — mercy with a memory, kept and guarded for thousands of generations, loyal beyond our failures.

note_body: Jacob readies his servants for Esau's asking — whose art thou, and whither goest thou — and in Judges a traveler meets that same evening question, whither goest thou. God's people answer best when worship, not fear, has already settled whose we are.
lens_gloss: to ask, inquire — the asking that tests identity; questions a heart can meet with settled, worship-formed answers.

note_body: Moses promises the far-off seeker will find God when the whole heart searches, and Joel calls for that same whole-heart turning with fasting and weeping. The Father wants honest return, not a performance of it.
lens_gloss: to seek, inquire after — careful, pursuing search; wholehearted reaching after God Himself rather than a display of piety.

note_title: Feed the ones who wounded you.
note_body: Joseph answers his brothers' fear with provision and heart-deep kindness, nourishing the very men who sold him, and Paul carries it forward — if thine enemy hunger, feed him. Mercy speaks loudest through a full table.
lens_gloss: to sustain, provide for — mercy that shows up as daily bread, care measured out even for the little ones.

note_body: God interrupts Abram's substitute arrangement with a word — the heir will come by promise, not improvisation. Paul says believers are, like Isaac, children of promise: born of what God speaks, not of what fear constructs.
lens_gloss: to inherit, take possession — the promised future received as God's gift, never secured by fear's arrangements.

note_body: At Sinai the Lord descends in holiness and calls Moses upward, and Paul marvels that Christ descended lower still before ascending. The holy God has never been too high to come down and call His people up.
lens_gloss: to come down, descend — the holy God's own downward movement toward His people before He calls them upward.

note_body: Jacob prays the promise back — thou saidst, I will surely do thee good — and through Isaiah the Lord invites exactly that: put me in remembrance. Covenant memory is not manipulation; it is prayer the Father Himself requested.
lens_gloss: to do good — doubled in the Hebrew, 'doing good I will do thee good,' a promise folded over itself for emphasis.

note_title: A psalm that rose at Pentecost.
note_body: David sings that even his flesh rests in hope, and Peter lifts the very same song at Pentecost over the risen Christ. The body's rest is anchored in a tomb that could not hold Him.
lens_gloss: security, safety — the settled ease of a body no longer braced for impact, resting at home in trust.

note_body: Egypt beholds Sarai as a beautiful thing to acquire, and Jesus traces that very gaze back to its root in the heart. Love learns to see people as beloved, never as merchandise.
lens_gloss: beautiful, fair — a God-given radiance meant to be honored, never fed to the appetite of power.

note_title: A name planted before the need.
note_body: Rebekah first appears tucked inside a quiet family report, long before anyone knows why she matters, and Paul later names her among the promise-bearers. God was preparing mercy generations ahead of the need.
lens_gloss: to bear, beget — the quiet generational verb by which God threads tomorrow's grace through today's family lines.

note_title: Awe, met by a steadying hand.
note_body: Moses hides his face before the God of his fathers, and John falls as dead until the risen Lord lays a hand on him — fear not, I am the first and the last. Holy awe is welcomed, then steadied by grace.
lens_gloss: to fear, revere — the fear that bows rather than flees; reverent awe before holiness, not the cringe of the rejected.

note_body: Moses names the danger of a heart that turns and stops listening, and Hebrews carries the same plea — refuse not him that speaketh. The Father warns not to frighten His children but to keep them near.
lens_gloss: to turn, face away — the heart's quiet pivot from God, which love names honestly before it hardens into distance.

note_body: Jacob, greatly afraid, splits everything he loves into two camps against expected loss, and Paul points anxiety toward a better strategy — in every thing, by prayer with thanksgiving, hand the fear to God before it runs the plans.
lens_gloss: to be pressed, cramped into a narrow place — Scripture's word for distress, the squeeze fear puts on the heart.

note_body: Sarai is appraised, commended, and taken as if power settles everything, and Hebrews answers plainly — marriage is honourable, and God Himself will judge its violators. What the palace called normal, heaven called accountable.
lens_gloss: to take — here in the passive, a woman taken by power; Scripture records the seizure honestly and holds it before God.

note_body: At Sinai the people answer together after grace has been recited; at Shechem a new generation does the same, saying yes to the God who already carried them. The order never changes — deliverance first, then the answer.
lens_gloss: to answer, respond — Israel's yes is not an opening bid but a reply; grace always speaks the first word.

note_title: A true thing, bent by fear.
note_body: Abram sees something true about Sarai, and fear immediately starts drafting a plan around it. Proverbs names the whole mechanism: the fear of man lays the snare, and trust in the LORD is the door out of it.
lens_gloss: beautiful, fair — a genuine good in Sarai that fear seizes and bends into a plan; the truth itself was never the danger.

note_title: Named at the margins, kept forever.
note_body: Genesis pauses its great story to keep Reumah's name, and Proverbs tells us why: the LORD Himself establishes the border of the widow. Heaven guards the very people the world files under footnotes.
lens_gloss: name — in Scripture a kept name is a kept person; heaven's record holds the people the world reads past.

note_body: Moses says God set His heart on the fathers before there was anything impressive to show for it, and Peter hands the church the same word — chosen, called out of darkness. Belonging comes before shining, in both Testaments.
lens_gloss: to cling to in love, to set one's heart on — God's delight fastened itself to the fathers before anything impressive existed.

note_body: Abram hands Sarai her lines so that he will be safe, and centuries later Peter draws back from the Gentile table under the same pressure. Fear of man can bend even pillars — which is why grace, not performance, has to hold us up.
lens_gloss: soul, life, the whole self — Abram guards his own nefesh by exposing another's; fear always miscounts what a life is worth.

note_body: Israel asks on the shore who is like the LORD, glorious in holiness, and Revelation shows the answer still rising day and night before the throne. The song fear cannot survive is the one heaven never stops singing.
lens_gloss: holiness, set-apartness — what makes the LORD unmatched among every rival power; fear shrinks wherever the Holy One is beheld.

note_body: Abram rehearses the scene — they will kill me — and starts scripting his own survival. Jesus takes up that very fear and sets it under a greater keeping: the ones who can kill the body cannot touch the soul.
lens_gloss: to kill — the word Abram's imagination keeps rehearsing; Jesus lifts that same word out of the seat of decision.

note_body: Joseph kisses and weeps before his brothers manage a single word, and the prodigal's father runs and kisses before the rehearsed confession is finished. Mercy touches first, and that is what makes talking possible again.
lens_gloss: to kiss — the sign of peace given before the brothers can find words; affection opens the door that speech walks through.

note_body: The song at the sea ends with planting, and God's word to David turns it into a promise: a place of their own, moved no more. Deliverance in Scripture always carries an address.
lens_gloss: to plant — redemption's finish line is not escape but rootedness; the Redeemer settles His people where He Himself dwells.

note_title: Escorts sent before the hard road.
note_body: Jacob is met by the angels of God while Esau is still down the road, and Hebrews names what he saw: ministering spirits sent for the heirs of salvation. Reassurance travels ahead of reconciliation.
lens_gloss: to meet, encounter — heaven intercepts Jacob on the road before Esau can; mercy reaches him first.

note_body: Abram builds an altar on land he does not yet possess, and Hebrews tells us the shape of that heart — he obeyed and went out, not knowing where. Faith answers a promise with worship, not with a completed map.
lens_gloss: altar — a built answer to a spoken promise; worship marks ground that faith has not yet seen fulfilled.

note_body: Moses promises a God who gathers His people from every nation where they were scattered, and Isaiah hears the same heart say east and west. Scattering has never once made the Father lose track of His own.
lens_gloss: to gather, collect — compassion that does not merely pity the scattered but goes out and brings them home.

note_body: God creates the great creatures of the deep and calls them good, and the psalmist summons the dragons and all deeps into the choir. Nothing in your depths is outside His mercy or His music.
lens_gloss: to create — a verb Scripture reserves for God alone; even the deep, strange, and unnamed come from His hand and are called good.

note_title: A gift shaped in the dark.
note_body: Jacob spends the night turning prayer into a concrete present for Esau, and Proverbs blesses the instinct: a gift makes room. Mercy that has been prepared opens doors that panic never could.
lens_gloss: gift, offering, tribute — the same word used for offerings brought to God; Jacob's prepared gesture turns fear into humble giving.

note_body: Moses at the bush and Joshua outside Jericho hear the same word: take off your shoes. Reverence was never one man's moment — it is how every generation draws near to mercy.
lens_gloss: ground, soil — ordinary dust under Moses' feet made holy because God is present there; reverence begins where He stands.

note_body: Jacob sends word ahead, asking to find grace in his brother's eyes, and Ruth walks into the field with the same hope on her lips. The humble ask first, and favor makes room before they arrive.
lens_gloss: grace, favor — what Jacob asks for instead of grasping; the humble word that goes ahead and makes room.

note_body: Genesis gives Jacob's obedience one plain line — he listened and he went — and Paul gives children the same breath: obey, for this is right. Listening becomes love when it starts walking.
lens_gloss: to hear, hearken — in Hebrew, real hearing includes obeying; listening worth the name completes itself in the feet.

note_body: Ruth asks why Boaz would notice a foreigner, and Elisabeth asks why her Lord's mother would come to her door. Grace keeps astonishing the very people who assumed they would always stand at the edge.
lens_gloss: foreigner, outsider — the name Ruth still uses for herself even while grace is quietly rewriting it.

note_title: The waters still know His voice.
note_body: At creation one command gathers the waters so firm ground can appear, and on Galilee the same voice makes wind and water obey. What feels scattered in you is not beyond His gathering word.
lens_gloss: to be gathered, collected — scattered waters drawn to one place at a word, until firm standing ground appears.

note_title: Obedience in the bone of today.
note_body: Abraham obeys in the selfsame day the word arrives, and the psalmist confesses the secret of such a life: I made haste, and delayed not. Obedience is sweetest while the day is still speaking.
lens_gloss: bone, very substance — 'in the bone of that day': obedience carried out in the marrow of the same day it was commanded.

note_body: David's cry rises from distress straight into God's ears, and Jonah's prayer climbs from the belly of the fish to the same holy temple. There is no depth from which the cry cannot reach Him.
lens_gloss: distress, a narrow place — the tight squeeze where prayer is born, and from which the cry still reaches God's ears.

note_body: Genesis shows God dividing light from darkness and calling the order good; Jeremiah points to those same steady ordinances as the pledge that His covenant love will not waver. The God of order can be trusted with your mixtures.
lens_gloss: to separate, distinguish — God lovingly sorts light from darkness rather than leaving life blurred; His order is mercy, not severity.

note_title: Addressed to the house of Jacob.
note_body: Sinai's message is addressed to the house of Jacob — a family named for a wrestler — and Paul later inventories their treasure: the adoption, the covenants, the promises. A complicated history has never disqualified anyone from being personally addressed.
lens_gloss: to call, summon by name — God's word arrives addressed, not broadcast; He calls a family whose whole story He knows.

note_title: The chair only God can fill.
note_body: Joseph quiets his brothers' terror by refusing to sit where only God sits, and Paul hands the church the same freedom: give place unto wrath. The verdict was never ours to carry.
lens_gloss: in the place of, instead of — Joseph refuses the seat that belongs to God alone; peace begins where self-appointed judgment ends.

note_body: Joseph's forgiveness arrives with wagons, households, and the fat of the land, and the psalm sings the same character: peace in the borders and the finest of the wheat. Real mercy feeds people.
lens_gloss: fat, the richest portion — mercy does not hand out leftovers; restored love spreads a table with the best of the land.

note_body: Moses anchors hope in who God is — merciful, unable to forget His covenant — and Hezekiah's runners carry that word to a scattered generation: return, and His face will not turn away. Correction is a hallway home, not a locked door.
lens_gloss: compassionate — kin to the Hebrew word for womb; God's mercy carries the fierce tenderness of a mother toward her child.

note_body: Jacob watches heaven's traffic descend to a fugitive who arranged none of it, and Jesus tells Nathanael the ladder's name: the angels ascend and descend on the Son of man. Mercy comes down first.
lens_gloss: ladder, stairway — a word appearing only here in all Scripture; heaven builds the connection down to Jacob, not the reverse.

note_body: The brothers cannot risk coming close, so they send words wrapped in their father's authority, and Paul models what such fear is waiting to hear — a father's voice that exhorts and comforts in the same breath. Gentle clarity is how mercy answers a trembling message.
lens_gloss: to charge, command — the brothers lean on their father's charge; fearful hearts often borrow words before they can risk their own.

note_body: At the bush God says, 'I will stretch out my hand'; in Stephen's sermon that same hand is history — 'He brought them out.' Fear shrinks when the promise you are holding has already been kept once in public.
lens_gloss: wonders, marvelous deeds beyond human reach — the same word the psalms use for God's acts worth retelling to children.

note_body: Isaac's word to Jacob is all verbs — arise, go, take — and Hosea remembers what those verbs cost: years of keeping sheep for the wife he was sent to find. Mercy's next step is rarely glamorous, but it is walkable.
lens_gloss: arise, stand up — Scripture's word for the moment resolve stops being a feeling and becomes motion.

note_body: A horror of great darkness falls on Abram the very night God binds Himself to him, and darkness falls on Saul at the very hour Christ claims him. In both stories the lights go down because God is nearer, not farther.
lens_gloss: a God-sent deep sleep — the helpless stillness in which the Lord works while a man can add nothing.

note_title: The mark that sets a table.
note_body: Genesis puts the covenant sign on everyone in the house, born or bought, and Exodus shows why: once marked, the servant sits down to the Passover with the family. Belonging that stops at the door was never God's version.
lens_gloss: covenant — a binding bond of belonging, here carried in the flesh of every member of the household, forever.

note_body: Deuteronomy is remembering the morning Exodus records — right after the calf, God does not cancel the trip. 'Depart, and go up' is what mercy sounds like when it refuses to leave you parked in your failure.
lens_gloss: to take possession, to inherit — mercy's forward motion has an address, land already sworn and waiting.

note_body: Pharaoh's mercy arrives as logistics — load the animals, take the road, come back for your father. Deuteronomy keeps the receipt: do not abhor the Egyptian, for you were a stranger in his land, and kindness has a long memory.
lens_gloss: to do, to make — Pharaoh's 'this do ye' turns mercy into a verb that hands and pack animals can carry out.

note_body: The brothers say it plainly — 'they did unto thee evil' — and Joseph weeps instead of striking. At the cross the same grammar returns: real evil, fully named, answered with 'Father, forgive them.'
lens_gloss: to lift, bear, carry away — forgiveness pictured as stooping to pick a weight up off another's back.

note_body: At Marah God introduces Himself: 'I am the LORD that healeth thee.' In Matthew's crowded evening that name is standing in a doorway, and every sick soul they carry to Jesus meets Him.
lens_gloss: to heal, mend, stitch back together — here folded into God's own name: the LORD your Healer.

note_title: Bowed like slaves, kept like family.
note_body: Joseph's brothers fall down offering to be servants, sure that mercy has run out. David answers that same trembling posture in Mephibosheth — 'Fear not... thou shalt eat bread at my table continually' — because covenant kindness seats people, it does not sentence them.
lens_gloss: servant, bond-slave — the brothers volunteer for chains while Joseph, and God, keep insisting on family.

note_body: Abram's careful arranging looks obscure until Jeremiah names the rite: those who cut the calf and passed between the parts were staking their lives on their word. Abram was not doing busywork; he was setting the table for God's own oath.
lens_gloss: to cut in two — the covenant-cutting verb; a promise made solemn by pieces laid opposite each other.

note_title: The cry that reaches the throne.
note_body: Exodus says Israel's cry 'is come unto me'; James says the cheated field workers' wages cry too, and the cries have 'entered into the ears of the Lord of sabaoth.' Before God sends anyone anywhere, He has already heard everything.
lens_gloss: the raw outcry of the wronged — a cry Scripture insists travels the whole distance to God's ear.

note_body: Stephen keeps Genesis' order intact: God 'gave him the covenant,' and Abraham's obedience came after, as answer rather than audition. Keeping covenant is how the found heart says thank You, not how it applies for the position.
lens_gloss: to keep, guard, watch over — covenant tended like something precious entrusted, not performed like a test to pass.

note_body: Genesis gives Abram's day one quiet line — he kept journeying south. Hebrews frames that unphotogenic faithfulness as glory: strangers and pilgrims who saw the promises afar off and kept walking anyway.
lens_gloss: to pull up tent pegs and set out again — faith wearing its plainest clothes, another day's walking.

note_title: The book opens when you turn.
note_body: Deuteronomy will not separate the written law from a turned heart, and Paul says why: 'when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away.' Return is what makes reading become meeting.
lens_gloss: to turn around, to come home — the Old Testament's great repentance word, a returning more than a resolution.

note_body: Genesis records the step — 'So Abram departed, as the LORD had spoken.' Hebrews opens the seam and shows the lining: by faith he obeyed and went out, not knowing whither, which is what promises are for.
lens_gloss: to walk, to go — the Bible's simplest faith verb: Abram heard, and Abram walked.

note_title: A stone pillow, a homeless King.
note_body: Jacob lays his head on a rock in a nowhere place and wakes at the gate of heaven. The Son of man had not where to lay His head either — God has a long habit of turning unpromising ground into meeting places.
lens_gloss: place — an ordinary patch of ground that becomes, once God stands in it, the very house of God.

note_body: Before Moses lifts a finger, God has already named the rescue and the destination — 'I will bring you up... unto a land flowing with milk and honey.' Paul knows this same God: faithful, and already making the way to escape.
lens_gloss: to go up; 'I will bring you up' — the climb out of affliction announced as God's own doing first.

note_title: The call took the household along.
note_body: Abram's obedience travels heavy — wife, nephew, goods, and souls gathered in Haran — and Stephen retells it through a father's death and a family's slow move. The call does not wait for an uncomplicated life, and Canaan was reached anyway.
lens_gloss: soul, a living person — obedience here travels with actual lives, whole persons gathered into the going.

note_body: Isaac bound on the wood is never a license for human hands; it is a window. In the garden the true beloved Son let them bind Him, so that the cost of the altar would land on God's own heart and not on ours.
lens_gloss: to bind — the rare, weighty verb that names this scene the Akedah, the binding of the beloved son.

note_body: The psalmist tells the LORD, 'Thou art my Lord' — my good is not apart from You. Thomas, standing close enough to touch the wounds, says the rest of it: 'My Lord and my God.'
lens_gloss: my Lord, my Master — the soul's glad word of ownership: I am not my own, and would not be.

note_title: Over the brook, into God's keeping.
note_body: Jacob sends everything he has across the water and stands empty-handed in the dark, which is exactly where God meets him. Peter gives that motion its name: casting all your care upon Him, for He careth for you.
lens_gloss: to cross over — Jacob makes all he loves pass beyond his grip, release enacted at a stream in the dark.

note_title: Known by name, led by name.
note_body: God answers Moses from personal acquaintance — 'thou hast found grace... I know thee by name.' Jesus says His flock lives there daily: the Shepherd calls His own sheep by name, and leads them out.
lens_gloss: to know personally and intimately — not information about you, but acquaintance with you, name and all.

note_body: Abraham's obedience looks like saddling a donkey and splitting wood at first light. The psalmist knows that shape by heart: 'I made haste, and delayed not to keep thy commandments.'
lens_gloss: to rise early, at first light — Scripture's quiet signal of obedience that does not wait for feelings to gather.

note_body: Genesis appoints a greater light and a lesser light and hangs the stars without apology. Paul turns it into comfort for compared-out hearts: one glory of the sun, another of the moon — each shining exactly as assigned.
lens_gloss: light-bearer, lamp — each luminary made to carry its own assigned measure of shining, without rivalry.

note_body: What Moses gave Israel as its daily creed, Jesus names the first commandment of all. Two Testaments agree on the arithmetic: love for God takes the whole heart, soul, and strength — pieces were never the currency.
lens_gloss: 'muchness' — everywhere else the little word for 'very'; here, love God with all your very-ness, nothing held back.

note_body: Abraham sees the place afar off with the hardest steps still ahead, and Hebrews tells us what carried him: he accounted that God was able to raise the dead. Unfinished is not the same as abandoned.
lens_gloss: to see — Moriah's key verb; 'the LORD will provide' in this story literally reads 'the LORD will see.'

note_title: Refused by men, sent by God.
note_body: Joseph renames his brothers' betrayal with God's verb — 'God sent me before you to preserve life.' Stephen traces the same pattern in Moses: the very man they refused, God sent to deliver.
lens_gloss: to send — Joseph retells his betrayal with God's verb: not 'they sold me' but 'He sent me before you.'

note_body: The song born on the far side of the Red Sea never stops; Revelation hears the redeemed still singing it — the song of Moses and of the Lamb. Every remembered deliverance teaches the morning its melody.
lens_gloss: song, to sing — deliverance's first language; the far shore of the sea gives Israel a music it never loses.

note_title: What Abraham was spared, God carried.
note_body: On Moriah heaven stopped Abraham's hand before the beloved was lost; at Calvary the Father did not stop His own. The God who asks for your dearest thing has already given up His.
lens_gloss: your only one — the word for a singular, irreplaceable beloved; the very treasure God asks us to entrust to His character.

note_title: A field made sure, a shoe given.
note_body: Abraham's field was made sure before the sons of Heth, and Ruth's redemption was sealed with a sandal passed hand to hand. God's people have always let grace be confirmed where witnesses can see it.
lens_gloss: attestation, testimony — redemption sealed by a witnessed act; surrender confirmed in public, not left as a private intention.

note_title: The Father of lights keeps time.
note_body: The One who hung lights to govern signs and seasons is named in James the Father of lights, with no shadow of turning. The hands that order your calendar do not waver with it.
lens_gloss: appointed time — the lights mark set meetings, not vague seasons; God keeps a calendar of faithful appointments.

note_title: Ninety-nine years, and grace still counted.
note_body: Paul looks at that ninety-nine-year-old obedience and calls it a seal of faith already counted, making Abraham father of all who believe. What looked late became the doorway for every latecomer after him.
lens_gloss: to circumcise — the covenant mark; received in ninety-nine-year-old flesh, proof that God's present call outruns 'too late.'

note_title: The feared face calls them close.
note_body: Joseph's brothers stood troubled before the face they had wronged, and Moses' leaders returned to a face still shining from the mountain. Both times the presence they feared called them near to hear mercy speak.
lens_gloss: to call, summon — restoration begins with a voice calling the distant back within hearing range.

note_title: The Maker's hands, the Maker's right.
note_body: The God who made beast and cattle after their kind tells Jeremiah He formed earth, man, and animal by His outstretched arm and gives as He sees fit. Hands that deliberate are hands a heart can yield to.
lens_gloss: to make, fashion — the Maker's deliberate handiwork; what His hands form, His eyes call good.

note_title: The Tester already knows the ending.
note_body: God tested Abraham, and Jesus tested Philip — 'for he himself knew what he would do.' The test is never a question about God's provision, only an invitation to answer, Here am I.
lens_gloss: to test, prove — a refining that assumes worth; God proves hearts He already plans to provide for.

note_title: Brought out, and truly brought in.
note_body: Deuteronomy says He brought them out on purpose to bring them in; Jeremiah, generations later, prays over land actually given, flowing with milk and honey. God finishes His sentences.
lens_gloss: to bring in — deliverance's destination word; the going out was always for the sake of a bringing in.

note_title: Awe met by a steadying hand.
note_body: Jacob wakes trembling at the gate of heaven, and John falls as dead before the glory — until a right hand rests on him with 'Fear not.' Holy dread, met rightly, ends in touch rather than banishment.
lens_gloss: awesome, fear-inspiring — trembling wonder at God's nearness; a dread that draws close rather than drives away.

note_body: Abraham and Ishmael received the mark in the selfsame day, and the psalmist made haste and delayed not to keep the commandments. Prompt surrender gathers in the people standing nearest to us.
lens_gloss: bone, very substance — 'the selfsame day' means the very bone of the day; obedience that does not postpone.

note_title: Promised at the bush, sung later.
note_body: At the bush God promised the women would ask and not leave empty-handed; the psalmist looks back and sings that they came out with silver and gold, not one feeble among them. Provision was planned before the road was walked.
lens_gloss: to ask — the word behind 'borrow'; provision received by simple asking from a God who planned the road.

note_title: Drive the birds from the seed.
note_body: Abram drove the fowls from the covenant pieces, and Jesus tells of fowls that devour the seed sown by the wayside. Part of keeping the yes is standing guard over what God has laid out.
lens_gloss: bird of prey — the scavenger that circles what is consecrated; some faithfulness is simply driving it away.

note_body: In the wilderness, hunger repainted the slave-house flesh pots as good eating; Joseph's loaded donkeys show what true provision looks like — the good things of Egypt sent in love for the road home. Mercy provides; fear only misremembers.
lens_gloss: the good, the best of — mercy does not send leftovers; the road home is loaded with the finest.

note_body: At Sinai the people washed their garments to stand before the Lord; Hebrews calls us to draw near with bodies washed and hearts sprinkled, in full assurance. Preparation has always been mercy making room for nearness.
lens_gloss: to set apart as holy — consecration as mercy's preparation, making a beloved people ready to draw near rightly.

note_body: Over creation God saw everything He had made and called it very good; over Galilee the crowds marveled, 'He hath done all things well.' The same hands, the same unhurried finishing.
lens_gloss: good — crowned here as tov me'od, very good; the Maker's settled, unhurried verdict over finished work.

note_title: Grief learns the way to thrones.
note_body: Mordecai's sackcloth could not pass the king's gate, and Joseph waited until the days of mourning were past before asking Pharaoh's house to speak for him. Grief is honored first; then the humble request finds its voice.
lens_gloss: grace, favor — Joseph, for all his power, asks on the footing of favor, not demand; humble requests stand on grace.

note_title: The return already has a runner.
note_body: Deuteronomy calls the wanderer home with all the heart and soul; Luke shows what waits at the end of that road — a father running, embracing, kissing the returner before a word of explanation. The turn is ours; the running is His.
lens_gloss: to turn, return — Scripture's great repentance word; not self-improvement but a whole-heart turning toward home.

note_body: Over a runaway asleep on a stone God says, 'to thee and to thy seed'; Paul reads that word and names the Seed — Christ Himself. The promise spoken on Jacob's road was always traveling somewhere.
lens_gloss: seed — one small word carrying generations; a promise wide enough to reach from Jacob's pillow to Christ.

note_body: The brothers went up from Egypt carrying word that Joseph was yet alive, and the women returned from the tomb carrying news of the same shape. Some homecomings exist to revive a grieving heart.
lens_gloss: to go up — the Bible's direction word for returning to the land; homecoming is always an ascent.

note_body: What God promised Moses — mercy on whom I will have mercy — Paul carries word for word into Romans. Grace was never a formula to master, only a goodness that passes near.
lens_gloss: to be gracious, show favor — doubled in God's own mouth; grace answering to no formula, only to His heart.

note_title: Near unto me, says the redeemer.
note_body: Joseph settles his family in Goshen with the words 'thou shalt be near unto me'; Jesus prays that His own would be with Him where He is. Redemption has never been satisfied with rescue at a distance.
lens_gloss: near — not mere distance but belonging; the redeemer arranges a place within reach of his daily care.

note_title: The law kept a door open.
note_body: Leviticus provided that a kinsman could redeem what a poor brother lost, so when the nearer kinsman said 'I cannot,' the provision still stood waiting. One man's no could not close a door God had written open.
lens_gloss: to redeem as kinsman — to buy back what belongs to family; a right only the willing can carry.

note_title: Encounters that mark the walk after.
note_body: Israel kept a table practice from the hollow of Jacob's thigh, and Israel kept a place-name from the breach at Perez-uzza. Real encounters with God leave marks that instruct the walk of those who come after.
lens_gloss: thigh, hip — the seat of strength that wrestling touched; a changed walk became a kept remembrance.

note_body: A very great company went up with Joseph to bury his father, and devout men carried Stephen with great lamentation. In both Testaments, faithful grief is surrounded, witnessed, and never made to travel alone.
lens_gloss: heavy, weighty — sharing a root with 'glory'; sorrow carried with weight, honor, and great company.

note_body: Israel walked three days through the wilderness of Shur and found no water; in that same Shur the angel of the LORD once found Hagar sitting by a fountain. The God who sees already knows where the water is.
lens_gloss: wilderness — the land beyond planting where God alone provides; even after miracles the road passes through it.

note_title: He passes by, unperceived at first.
note_body: Job confesses, 'he goeth by me, and I see him not,' and Jacob wakes to say the LORD was in this place and I knew it not. Looking back is often where beloved eyes first learn to recognize Him.
lens_gloss: to know — 'lo yadati,' I knew it not; awareness often arrives after the mercy has already been present.

note_body: Moses warned that full tables can turn hearts to other gods; the wise man turned that warning into a prayer — 'lest I be full, and deny thee.' Gratitude that hands the gift back keeps the Giver in view.
lens_gloss: to be full, satisfied — a good gift with a quiet danger; fullness that can forget the Giver.

note_title: The waters still know His voice.
note_body: In Genesis the word becomes a firmament and the waters take their appointed places; on Galilee the winds and the sea still obey that voice. What God speaks does not hover as intention — it takes form.
lens_gloss: expanse, firmament — something hammered out and set firmly in place; God's word takes form, not just intention.

note_title: The mountain ends in a hometown.
note_body: Abraham walks down from Moriah and settles in Beersheba, and generations later that same town frames Israel's gathered life, from Dan even to Beersheba. The ordinary places we faithfully return to become landmarks God builds His people around.
lens_gloss: to turn back, return — the same root Scripture uses for repentance; coming down the mountain is holy movement too

note_body: God answers Moses' 'Who am I?' with 'I will be with thee,' and the risen Jesus sends His disciples out on the very same credential. Presence, not a resume, is what carries the sent.
lens_gloss: 'I will be' — the very word God gives as His name two verses later; His presence is His identity

note_body: The God who gathered the seas and named the dry land is the same God Isaiah says gives breath to the people walking on it. The One who set boundaries around the waters can set them around your pressures too.
lens_gloss: to call, to name — when God names a thing, it finds its place, and peace follows His order

note_body: Paul lifts David's very words about the open-grave throat straight into Romans to show what every unguarded mouth can become. What David suffered from his enemies, grace alone keeps out of us.
lens_gloss: to be smooth, slippery — flattery is speech polished until truth slides right off it; test the shine

note_body: Abram falls on his face as covenant love draws near, and in Gethsemane the beloved Son takes the exact same posture. Falling forward before the Father is what trust looks like when His will is bigger than ours.
lens_gloss: to fall — not collapse but chosen lowering; the body telling the truth about who is holy and who is held

note_body: Jacob names bread and raiment on a lonely road, and Paul names food and raiment as reason enough for contentment. The plain needs we bring honestly are the very ones the Father counts worthy of His care.
lens_gloss: a vow — a spoken binding of the heart; even a learning tongue can offer God honest, unfinished trust

note_body: Moses says only God's going-with can mark a people as His own, and Matthew names the final answer Emmanuel, God with us. The distinction Moses begged for finally arrived wearing flesh.
lens_gloss: to be distinct, set apart — what makes God's people unmistakable is never performance, only His going with them

note_body: God tells a runaway with a stone for a pillow, 'I will not leave thee,' and Hebrews sets the same never-leaving promise over every believer. What steadied Jacob on the road still holds for us tonight.
lens_gloss: to leave, forsake — the word God negates over Jacob; His 'I will not' outlasts every mile of the road

note_body: Jacob coaches his messengers to say 'thy servant' before the brother he wronged, and Jesus states the law beneath it: the one who lowers himself is the one who gets lifted. Humble words walk ahead of us into hard rooms.
lens_gloss: servant — Jacob hands his swagger away in one word; humility speaks first so peace can enter the room

note_body: Moses tells Israel the word is already in their mouth and heart, and Paul quotes him to say the word of faith has come just as near. God has never played a game of distance with His people.
lens_gloss: near — not across the sea, not up in heaven; God sets His word within reach of mouth and heart

note_title: A marriage recorded, a promise unmoved.
note_body: Esau reaches into Ishmael's line to mend how things look, and Chronicles quietly files those same names into a genealogy. Appearances get recorded, but the promise keeps moving where God swore it would.
lens_gloss: to take — Esau's grasping verb; hands can take what only a surrendered heart can actually receive

note_body: Abram's famine road runs to Egypt and Naomi's runs to Moab, and God carries the promise through both detours — one toward a nation, the other toward a Moabite girl in David's line. Scarcity moves the beloved; it never unnames them.
lens_gloss: famine, hunger — the loud pressure that tests whether need or the God who named you gets the final word

note_title: The bush's miracle becomes your promise.
note_body: At Horeb the fire burns and the bush is not consumed, and through Isaiah God speaks that same mercy over His people walking through fire. The flame around you does not get the final say.
lens_gloss: the thornbush — common desert scrub; God chose the lowliest shrub in the wilderness to carry holy fire

note_body: Pharaoh's wagons roll out of Egypt for toddlers and an old father, and Isaiah sees kings turned into nursing fathers for God's returning children. When God restores, even worldly power gets borrowed to carry the weak gently.
lens_gloss: the little ones, the toddling ones — those who cannot march; God's restoration always budgets wagons for them

note_body: Abraham begs God not to overlook the son he already loves, and at Pentecost Peter announces a promise reaching to you, to your children, and to all afar off. The Father's covenant has room for the ones we carry in prayer.
lens_gloss: to live — a father's whole prayer packed into one verb, asking life for his boy before God's face

note_body: At the bush God says 'I am come down to deliver,' and in Jesus the same movement puts on flesh: 'I came down from heaven.' Heaven's answer to bondage has always been descent.
lens_gloss: to come down, descend — deliverance begins with God's downward movement toward the pain of His people

note_title: No one greater to swear by.
note_body: On Moriah God swears by His own self, and Hebrews explains the wonder of it — there was no one greater to swear by. The aftermath of your hardest test rests on God's own unchangeable name.
lens_gloss: to swear an oath — God stakes His own unchanging self as surety, so the aftermath rests on Him

note_title: See for yourselves; it is I.
note_body: Joseph lets his brothers' own eyes confirm it is really his mouth speaking peace, and the risen Jesus offers His hands and feet the same way. Restoring love does not mind being examined; it invites it.
lens_gloss: mouth — Joseph now speaks plainly, no interpreter between; reconciliation talks face to face in a familiar voice

note_body: Moses ties listening to living, and Jesus ties obeying to friendship. In both testaments, doing what God says is not hired labor — it is belonging to the One who loves you.
lens_gloss: to hear and heed — listening that becomes living; the same summons that opens Israel's beloved Shema

note_body: Joseph hurries his brothers home with 'come down, tarry not,' and centuries later Stephen retells that sending in his sermon. The prompt steps God asks of a rested heart become part of the salvation story He keeps telling.
lens_gloss: to hurry, hasten — mercy's urgency; feet can move quickly without striving when God has already made the way

note_body: Buz sits unnoticed in a family list until his descendant Elihu rises in the land of Uz to speak into Job's storm. The quiet names God records have a way of coming back carrying purpose.
lens_gloss: firstborn — the ordering word of family lines; God keeps careful track of the households we skim past

note_title: Sung at sea, fulfilled at Jordan.
note_body: Israel sings at the sea that Canaan's inhabitants will melt away, and forty years later Joshua records the kings' hearts melting exactly so. The fear moving through the land never had authority over the people God was carrying.
lens_gloss: to melt, dissolve — what hostile dread does before God; fear loses its solidity in His presence

note_body: Genesis shows God commanding the waters to teem with living things, and Paul tells Athens that same God still gives life and breath to all. The Giver has never once stopped giving movement.
lens_gloss: to swarm, teem — life bursting out in abundance at God's word; love does not empty the waters, it fills them

note_body: God promises Abram an afterward — judgment on the oppressor and a coming out with substance — and Stephen quotes those very words as accomplished history. What God names an afterward always arrives.
lens_gloss: to judge, vindicate — God's seeing turned into action; the oppressed have a court that never closes

note_title: The corners were left for her.
note_body: Ruth steps toward a stranger's field hoping to find grace, and Leviticus shows the grace was already written down — corners left uncut, gleanings left lying, signed 'I am the LORD your God.' Her humble step landed on prepared mercy.
lens_gloss: grace, favor — Ruth goes looking for it in a stranger's field and finds God's kindness already waiting

note_title: A road vow becomes a song.
note_body: On an uncertain road Jacob says 'then shall the LORD be my God,' and on the far shore of the sea his children sing 'my father's God, and I will exalt him.' Journeys that begin in fear can end in song.
lens_gloss: peace, wholeness — not merely safe arrival but a mended homecoming; what Jacob asks, God fully intends

note_body: At the bush God sees, hears, comes down, and only then says 'I will send thee' — and Stephen preaches that same order centuries later. True assignment always begins in God's compassion, never in our striving.
lens_gloss: to send — the commissioning verb; the one sent goes out carrying the Sender's own compassion and intention

note_body: Jacob counts out his peace offering goat by goat and ram by ram, and Deuteronomy names where such substance comes from — God gives power to get wealth for covenant's sake. The Father supplies so love has something concrete to hand over.
lens_gloss: she-goats, two hundred counted — love made concrete enough to number, herd, and hand over for peace's sake

note_title: The same voice, still speaking light.
note_body: Genesis hears God speak light over a dark deep; Paul says that very command has now shined in our hearts. The light you need today is not manufactured — it is spoken, and grace speaks first.
lens_gloss: light — the first created thing, spoken into being before any human hand existed to help or earn it.

note_title: He brings, He gathers, He restores.
note_body: Moses hears the Lord promise to bring His people in and do them good; Jeremiah hears the same God vow to gather His scattered ones home. Belonging always starts with His movement toward you, not your scramble toward Him.
lens_gloss: to do good, to make well — covenant goodness God performs Himself before His people lift a finger.

note_body: God introduces Himself to Abram as the One who already brought him out of Ur; Hebrews remembers that same road from Abram's side — he went out not knowing where, because he knew Who. Remembered faithfulness is fear's quietest cure.
lens_gloss: to bring out — God's remembered act of leading you out is the ground your next trust stands on.

note_body: Joseph promises to nourish his family through five lean years, and the women of Bethlehem bless Naomi with a nourisher for her old age — the very same Hebrew word. God's mercy keeps showing up as somebody's steady, practical provision.
lens_gloss: to sustain, to keep supplied — mercy measured out meal by meal, steady through every famine year.

note_title: A hand stretched out on purpose.
note_body: The song at the sea remembers the Lord's hand stretched out to end a threat; Isaiah says that same outstretched hand carries a settled purpose over all the earth. Your safety rests in strength that is never random.
lens_gloss: to stretch out — an arm extended in settled, saving purpose, never in panic.

note_title: Evening and morning, seed still growing.
note_body: Genesis closes each day of creation with a boundary, and Jesus tells of a farmer who sleeps and rises while the seed grows he knows not how. God keeps working inside the very rhythm that lets you stop.
lens_gloss: evening — in Hebrew reckoning the day begins at dusk, so rest opens the day before work does.

note_body: David asks how long he must counsel his own sorrowing heart; in the garden, Jesus speaks His soul's sorrow out loud and asks friends to stay near. Naming grief before God is not failing faith — it is faith.
lens_gloss: grief, heartache — the sorrow carried daily that the psalm lifts out of hiding and into God's hearing.

note_title: Two old houses, one appearing God.
note_body: God appears to ninety-nine-year-old Abram and calls him to walk before Him; Luke shows Zacharias and Elisabeth, old and childless, still walking blameless before God. In both houses the promise had not aged out — and the child came.
lens_gloss: the Almighty — the name of unfailing strength God speaks over a promise grown old in the waiting.

note_title: Two men of a hundred and ten.
note_body: Joseph dies at a hundred and ten with the promise still packed in an Egyptian coffin; Joshua dies at the same age buried inside the land itself. What one saint carries unfinished, God finishes in another's lifetime.
lens_gloss: a chest — the same word later names the ark of the covenant; even a coffin can carry a promise forward.

note_body: At the bush God promises His people will not leave empty, and the psalmist tallies the fulfillment — silver, gold, and not one feeble among the tribes. God restores dignity in particulars, not in generalities.
lens_gloss: favor, grace — worth placed on you in another's eyes because God Himself put it there.

note_title: He named it, He owns it.
note_body: In Genesis God names Day and Night the way a king titles his own estate; the psalmist simply rests there — the day is Thine, the night also is Thine. A Sabbath boundary is trust with a fence around it.
lens_gloss: to call, to name — time itself answers to the One who names it Day and Night.

note_body: Abraham brings thirteen-year-old Ishmael under the covenant sign though the boy's road ahead is uncertain; Hannah lends her long-prayed-for Samuel to the Lord for life. Love does its faithful part, then places the child in God's keeping.
lens_gloss: 'God hears' — the boy's own name preaching that the Father listens concerning the child you cannot control.

note_title: Love with food and clothing on it.
note_body: Moses says God loves the stranger with bread and raiment, and Hebrews hands us the apron — entertain strangers, for some have hosted angels unawares. The Father's practical love means to become practical in us.
lens_gloss: the sojourner — the outsider without kin or land whom God singles out for food, clothing, and love.

note_body: Abram asks the Lord how he will know, and Zacharias asks the very same question beside the altar. In both, God does not cancel the promise over an honest question — He seals it, and the child still comes.
lens_gloss: to know by lived experience — Abram asks for assurance he can stand on, and God answers with covenant, not scolding.

note_body: Jacob grapples with the man until daybreak; Hebrews shows Jesus in His own dark hours, praying with strong crying and tears — and heard. God is not offended by a struggle that refuses to let go of Him.
lens_gloss: to wrestle in the dust — a grappling close enough to leave you changed by the One who held you.

note_body: Israel sings of the right hand that broke an enemy's power, and Mary sings of the arm that scatters the proud. Centuries apart, God's people find their rest the same way — rehearsing His strength instead of straining their own.
lens_gloss: the right hand — strength in action; power that fights for you so your hands can finally rest.

note_body: Jacob's peace offering is itemized down to nursing camels traveling with their colts; Zacchaeus stands up and counts out restitution fourfold. Real care and real repentance both keep accounts — love shows up in the particulars.
lens_gloss: nursing mothers — Jacob's gift keeps mother animals with their young; compassion attentive even to the smallest traveler.

note_body: Jacob names his brother, his fear, and the children in danger; Jesus folds that same plain cry into the prayer He taught us — deliver us from evil. Specific prayer is not weak faith; it is faith telling the truth.
lens_gloss: to snatch away, to rescue — the cry that places a named danger into stronger hands.

note_body: Exodus tells what the Lord did with the water; Hebrews tells what Israel did — by faith they crossed as on dry land. Deliverance becomes identity when you keep standing on the ground God dried.
lens_gloss: dry ground — solid footing where sea floor should be; finished deliverance you can stand on.

note_body: Joseph says come near, then names the selling without flinching; Stephen retells it the same way — they sold him, but God was with him. Honest wounds and present grace can live in the same sentence.
lens_gloss: brother — the wound-word and the welcome-word in one; kinship reclaimed without denying the selling.

note_body: Israel is told to cut no covenant that would divide its heart, and Paul asks what communion light has with darkness. The old command's severity becomes the believer's clarity: an undivided heart is mercy to yourself.
lens_gloss: covenant — a binding of loyalties; some bonds must be refused so the first bond stays whole.

note_body: Pharaoh demands of Abram, what is this thou hast done; Joshua asks Achan the same question but begins with 'my son' and 'give glory to God.' In the Father's house, correction aims at confession that heals, not exposure that shames.
lens_gloss: to do — the question 'what hast thou done' calls hidden doing into the open, where mercy can meet it.

note_body: Abraham names the mountain The-LORD-Will-Provide, and trembling Gideon names his altar The-LORD-Is-Peace. Testimony turns geography into doctrine — the hard place now carries God's name instead of the fear's.
lens_gloss: to see, and therefore to provide — on Moriah God's look becomes supply, and the place bears His name.

note_body: At the bush Moses asks what name he should carry to a hurting people; in His great prayer Jesus says, I have manifested Thy name to those Thou gavest Me. What God answered in part at the bush, He answered in full in His Son.
lens_gloss: name — revealed character you can stand on when you are sent to speak for God.

note_body: Genesis pauses for names nobody preaches on, yet through quiet Bethuel comes Rebekah and the promise's next chapter; Jesus says even the hairs of your head are numbered. Nothing faithful is background to God.
lens_gloss: a quiet name ending in El, 'God' — the background father through whom Rebekah, and the promise, will come.

note_title: The neighbors named more than they knew.
note_body: The women of Bethlehem name a baby and recite three generations to David; Luke walks that same lineage back into Bethlehem when Joseph brings Mary home to register. Ordinary faithfulness had been carrying Christmas all along.
lens_gloss: 'serving' — the restoration baby is named Servant, and through his line come Jesse, David, and David's greater Son.

note_body: God lists the Rephaim to Abram as part of the promise itself; generations later Joshua points his people at that same giant country and says go up and clear it. What God names, He has already measured for you.
lens_gloss: the giant clans — even the largest named threat sits inside the borders of God's promise.

note_title: A place called Bitter, a woman too.
