note_body: Israel names the undrinkable water Marah, and Naomi comes home saying call me Mara. Neither gets scolded for honesty — and in both stories God is already on His way to sweeten what was truthfully named.
lens_gloss: bitter — Scripture lets the place wear its true name; honesty about bitterness is where sweetening begins.

note_title: Two men rose in the night.
note_body: Jacob gathers his family and crosses the Jabbok in the dark; Nehemiah rises in the night with only a few men and a burden God has laid on his heart. Some obedience cannot wait for morning, and God meets both men on the far side of it.
lens_gloss: to cross over, pass through — Scripture's word for a threshold obeyed; Jacob's night crossing could not be taken back.

note_title: The charge Moses gave, God repeated.
note_body: Moses tells Joshua "be strong and of a good courage" in the sight of all Israel; a few pages later God Himself speaks the same words to Joshua alone. When the human voice that steadied you goes silent, the Lord picks up the sentence.
lens_gloss: to be strong, take firm hold — courage in Hebrew is a grip, and God commands it because He Himself is what the hand holds.

note_body: Jacob renames Luz because God met him there, and generations on, Hosea says of that meeting, "there he spake with us." A place renamed by presence keeps preaching to children who never saw the ladder.
lens_gloss: house of God — ordinary ground renamed because the Lord was in this place; presence, not architecture, makes a house of God.

note_title: Honest lack is not lost confidence.
note_body: Abram lays his empty arms before God in plain words, and Hebrews urges the same nerve: cast not away your confidence. Naming the delay to His face is exactly how confidence stays alive.
lens_gloss: seed, offspring — the very word of God's promise, which Abram hands back to Him empty-handed and honest.

note_body: At the bush God says, "I have surely visited you," and generations later old Zechariah blesses the Lord who "hath visited and redeemed his people." The seeing that began in Egypt kept its appointment in Christ.
lens_gloss: to visit, attend to — doubled in the Hebrew, 'visiting I have visited': God's seeing that has already decided to act.

note_body: God told Abram plainly about four hundred years of strangerhood, and Stephen retells that very sentence on the far side of the exodus. A hard truth spoken in advance became proof that God knew the whole road all along.
lens_gloss: sojourner, resident stranger — a hard word spoken in advance, so that strangerhood could never be mistaken for abandonment.

note_body: David opens with "I will love thee, O LORD, my strength," and John tells us how such a song becomes possible: we love him because he first loved us. Deliverance taught David a melody mercy had written first.
lens_gloss: womb-deep, tender love — almost always God's compassion toward us; here, uniquely, David turns the word back to Him.

note_body: Joseph holds his brothers' evil and God's good in a single sentence, and Peter does the same when he preaches the cross at Pentecost: wicked hands, determinate counsel. Neither verse calls evil good; both watch God out-purpose it.
lens_gloss: to weave, plan, intend — the same verb for the brothers' plot and God's purpose: two designs on one loom, and God's held.

note_title: Tell my father of my glory.
note_body: Joseph sends word home: tell my father what you have seen, and bring him to me. Jesus prays the same homeward longing — that those the Father gave Him would be with Him and behold His glory.
lens_gloss: weight, honor, glory — good news with substance behind it, sturdy enough to carry an old father's hope down to Egypt.

note_title: The hard word became the testimony.
note_body: God tells Moses up front that Pharaoh will not bend easily, and Deuteronomy shows what that honesty grew into: parents telling children, "the LORD brought us out with a mighty hand." Truth named early becomes a story worth handing down.
lens_gloss: strong, hard — the word behind Pharaoh's hardened heart and, all through Exodus, for the mightier hand of God that breaks it.

note_body: Moses says keep your soul diligently, lest what your eyes have seen depart from your heart; Hebrews warns the church to give the more earnest heed, lest we let it slip. The memory of God's works is a treasure both testaments post a watchman over.
lens_gloss: to guard, keep watch — doubled here: guard yourself, guard your soul, the way a watchman keeps what is precious.

note_body: Joseph's brothers stand speechless and terrified before the one they wronged; the disciples cry out in fear at the figure on the water. In both rooms the troubling presence speaks first with mercy — it is I; be not afraid.
lens_gloss: to be terrified, struck speechless — the shock when hidden truth stands in the room, just before mercy opens its mouth.

note_title: The overcomer receives a new name.
note_body: Jacob limps out of his long night carrying the name Israel, because he prevailed. Revelation promises the same mercy to every overcomer — a new name in a white stone, given by the One who watched the whole struggle.
lens_gloss: to strive, persevere with — the verb folded inside the name Israel: the one who wrestled with God and did not let go.

note_body: Sinai says honor father and mother that your days may be long, and Paul carries the same command into the church, marking it as the first commandment with promise. God has never stopped attaching a future to how love moves through a family.
lens_gloss: to make weighty, treat as substantial — honor gives father and mother their true weight, the opposite of shallow politeness.

note_body: Jacob looks up on a tense road and recognizes God's host camped beside his own; the shepherds look up and the night fills with a multitude of the heavenly host. God's company has always been closer than the traveler knew.
lens_gloss: camp, company — Mahanaim means 'two camps': Jacob's small band, and God's unseen host pitched right beside it.

note_body: God pauses the conversation about Abraham to rename Sarai Himself, and Paul later builds his whole gospel picture on her — the freewoman whose son came by promise. The woman the story overlooked became the mother the promise required.
lens_gloss: princess — God Himself removes the old ending and speaks nobility over a woman the story had kept in the background.

note_title: Words moved from stone to heart.
note_body: Moses says these words shall be in thine heart; Paul says the Spirit now writes Christ's letter not with ink or on stone but on fleshy tables of the heart. What the law commanded, grace performs — God Himself doing the writing.
lens_gloss: heart — in Hebrew the seat of desire, memory, and will; the address where God intends His words to live, not visit.

note_body: Before the new name comes, Jacob has to say the old one out loud. Psalm 20 shows how far mercy carries that honesty — Heaven answers prayer under the title "the God of Jacob," the God who defends people by their truthful name.
lens_gloss: name — in Scripture a whole story carried in a word; God asks for it so the truth can stand in the light.

note_body: Moses measures himself against Pharaoh and comes up short, and God never argues the point. The Lord's answer to Paul is His answer at the bush: my grace is sufficient, and strength is made perfect in exactly that weakness.
lens_gloss: I — Moses's trembling 'who am I?' rests on this small word, and God quietly shifts the weight onto His own 'I will be.'

note_body: Paul quotes this very verse and names what God was doing all along: calling those things which be not as though they were. Abraham's name carried the multitude before Sarah ever carried the son.
lens_gloss: multitude, roaring abundance — folded into Abraham's new name before a single child of promise had been born.

note_body: "Abraham, Abraham" stops a knife; "Saul, Saul" stops a persecutor on the Damascus road. When heaven says the name twice, it is mercy interrupting a man deep in something he cannot see his way out of.
lens_gloss: 'here am I' — the servant's whole posture in one word: present, listening, and ready to be interrupted by mercy.

note_body: The enemy at the sea brags, "I will divide the spoil," and Jesus tells what happens when a stronger man arrives — the trusted armor is stripped and the spoils are divided the other way. Every pursuing voice eventually meets Someone stronger.
lens_gloss: to pursue, chase down — the enemy's boast at the sea; in Psalm 23 the same verb belongs to goodness and mercy.

note_title: Fear not; the Father delights to give.
note_body: God answers Abram's fear by becoming his shield and calling Himself the reward; Jesus answers ours the same way — fear not, little flock, for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom. The cure for fear is a Giver, not a guarantee.
lens_gloss: shield — not equipment God issues but what He Himself becomes, standing between Abram and everything he fears.

note_title: Leave the stuff; gain the land.
note_body: The word sent to Jacob's family is "regard not your stuff," because the good of the whole land waits ahead; Jesus promises that no one leaves house or lands for His sake without receiving more. Open hands only come easy when provision is already promised.
lens_gloss: goodness, the best of — a table already set farther down the road, making it safe to loosen the grip.

note_body: Deuteronomy promises the LORD will again rejoice over His restored people, and the father in Jesus' parable insists on the feast: it was meet that we should make merry. Heaven's welcome home comes with a joy the returning heart did not dare expect.
lens_gloss: to exult, delight — doubled in this verse: the LORD returning to rejoice over His people as He rejoiced over their fathers.

note_title: Words, wagons, and a sent brother.
note_body: Jacob's spirit revives when Joseph's words arrive with wagons he can see; Paul sends Epaphroditus in person so the Philippians' joy can have a face. Mercy loves to pair its message with something the weary can look at.
lens_gloss: to live, revive — Jacob's spirit 'came alive' when mercy's words arrived with wagons his old eyes could see.

note_body: Jacob coaches his servants to say "thy servant Jacob" and "my lord Esau" before the brothers ever stand face to face; Daniel addresses a fearsome king with the same costly courtesy before hard truth. Mercy chooses its tone ahead of time.
lens_gloss: gift, tribute, offering — the same word used for offerings brought to God; Jacob's peace-gift travels ahead like worship.

note_title: Led by mercy, kept by power.
note_body: The song at the sea says mercy led the redeemed and strength guided them to God's holy habitation; Peter says the redeemed are still kept by the power of God unto a salvation ready to be revealed. The love that leads you out is the power that walks you all the way in.
lens_gloss: steadfast covenant love — not a passing mood but a bound promise, strong enough to lead a whole people home.

note_title: Peace spoken over a whole life.
note_body: God tells Abram how his story will end before the middle has even unfolded, and old Simeon, cradling the promised Child, departs in that very peace. The Lord's assurance covers the whole road, not just the rough patch.
lens_gloss: wholeness, well-being, peace — God speaks shalom not over one crisis but over the entire length of Abram's road home.

note_body: Jacob splits his camp with a fear-taught shrewdness, and Jesus sends His own out wise as serpents yet harmless as doves. The Father does not strip the plan away; He steadies the trembling hands that made it.
lens_gloss: camp, company — the word from Mahanaim, where God's camp met Jacob's; even his fear-divided camps sit inside God's.

note_body: David sings of mercy promised to his seed for evermore, and Paul says it plainly: what God gives and calls, He never takes back. The love that sends you today carries no expiration date.
lens_gloss: covenant loyal-love — mercy bound by promise, not mood; the steadfast kindness God keeps moving toward David's line for evermore.

note_body: God answers Abraham with a named son, and centuries later an angel hands Zacharias the very same sentence — thy wife shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name. When the Lord redirects, He is specific, and He is kind.
lens_gloss: 'he laughs' — the promised son's name keeps Abraham's stunned laughter; God folds even our doubt into the shape of joy.

note_title: The hand stopped, the promise held.
note_body: The voice from heaven stays Abraham's hand, and Hebrews looks back to see what held that morning together — the promises, and a father receiving his son back alive. Mercy interrupts, and then mercy provides.
lens_gloss: the slaughter-knife — Scripture names the blade without flinching, so the mercy that stops it shines all the brighter.

note_body: Naomi blesses the kindness that never let go of the living or the dead, and Paul asks the church to hand that same tenderheartedness on. Kindness received is meant to become kindness practiced.
lens_gloss: kinsman-redeemer — the relative with the right to buy back what was lost; kindness that carries legal standing and a name.

note_body: Joseph and Joshua both close their journeys at one hundred and ten, servants whose last chapters were quiet faithfulness rather than spectacle. Sometimes the deepest mercy is a settled life that simply keeps serving.
lens_gloss: to sit, dwell, remain — Joseph's mercy settles into staying; grace that stops being an event and becomes an address.

note_body: Before Moses opens his mouth to Pharaoh, the message is already fixed: the God of the Hebrews hath met with us. Even Balaam knew to step aside and meet the Lord before risking a word to a king — presence comes before speech.
lens_gloss: to meet, encounter — Israel's first word to power is testimony, not argument: the God of the Hebrews has met with us.

note_body: Jacob gives the identical charge to the second messenger, the third, and all who follow, and Paul tells the Philippians that writing the same things is no trouble to him — for them it is safe. Mercy worth sending once is worth sending again.
lens_gloss: word, matter — 'on this manner' is literally 'according to this word'; one word of peace carried whole by every messenger.

note_title: An outward mark, an inward work.
note_body: Abraham's household receives a mark in the flesh, and Paul names the deeper cutting it always pointed toward — a circumcision made without hands, done quietly by Christ. The sign never made God faithful; it bore witness that He already was.
lens_gloss: covenant — the binding bond God himself cuts; the sign marks the promise, but the promise rests on the Promiser.

note_title: Sworn to fathers, kept in Christ.
note_body: Moses says the Lord keeps unto His people the covenant and mercy He swore to their fathers, and Zacharias sings the arrival of that very keeping — mercy promised, then performed. Obedience is simply how we walk around inside a love already sworn.
lens_gloss: to keep, guard — the same verb twice over: you keep His judgments, He keeps covenant mercy; keeping answers keeping.

note_title: A king reproved, a family spared.
note_body: The psalmist remembers this very scene when he sings that God reproved kings for His pilgrims' sakes. Abram had tangled the truth, yet mercy still escorted his whole household out of danger.
lens_gloss: to send out — the verb a later Pharaoh will learn with Israel; Abram's escorted exit quietly rehearses the Exodus.

note_body: Jacob raises an oiled pillar and Samuel raises an Ebenezer, and both stones do the same holy work — planting mercy where tomorrow's eyes can find it. Hitherto hath the LORD helped us.
lens_gloss: standing-stone, pillar — memory given a place to stand, so morning feet do not walk off from night mercy.

note_title: The sea song and the white horse.
note_body: Miriam's shore and John's opened heaven behold the same Lord, the One who judges and makes war in righteousness. From Egypt to the end of the book, His fight has always been for His people, not against them.
lens_gloss: battle, war — sung by freed slaves at the sea; the Lord's warfare is mercy in armor for people who could not fight.

note_body: Genesis records the command with no map attached, and Hebrews tells us what carried Abram out the door anyway — he obeyed, not knowing whither he went. Faith trusts the One who shows the land more than the eyes that cannot yet see it.
lens_gloss: 'go forth, for yourself' — a leaving commanded for Abram's own blessing; the road away from the familiar runs toward the promise.

note_title: Clear the room, gain the brother.
note_body: Joseph empties the room before truth and tears reach his brothers, and Jesus teaches that same tenderness — go to your brother alone first, and you may gain him. Some reconciliations need privacy before they can bear witnesses.
lens_gloss: to know — here reflexive, 'made himself known'; reconciling mercy is not complete until it steps out and lets itself be known.

note_body: Genesis sets a table for every creature that carries breath, and Psalm 104 watches the Father still setting it — grass for the cattle, herb for the service of man. The hand that has fed every living thing has surely not overlooked you.
lens_gloss: breath, living self — every creature carrying nephesh stands on the Father's provision list; His attention runs wider than our worry.

note_body: What Deuteronomy commands, Romans announces accomplished — a circumcision of the heart, in the spirit, with praise that comes from God alone. The Father's welcome includes the tender surgery that His welcome makes safe.
lens_gloss: heart — the willing, deciding center; God's tender knife aims past behavior to the guarded core He longs to soften.

note_title: Peniel now, face to face then.
note_body: Jacob limps from Peniel astonished that he saw God's face and lived, and Paul promises a fuller morning — no more dim glass, but face to face, fully known. The grace that preserved Jacob is the grace that will finish us.
lens_gloss: face, presence — Peniel means 'face of God'; grace is surviving the Face no striving could ever earn the right to see.

note_body: Paul calls the word spoken over Abraham's line the gospel preached beforehand — in thee shall all nations be blessed. The promise that found Jacob alone on a stone pillow was never meant to stop at one traveler's survival.
lens_gloss: family, clan — blessing measured in households; the promise travels kitchen to kitchen until it reaches every family on earth.

note_title: The same formula, leading with mercy.
note_body: When Israel's sin is at its worst, Moses pleads by quoting this very self-description — but he leads with longsuffering and great mercy. The jealous God guards His people the way a faithful husband guards a home.
lens_gloss: jealous — used only of God; a covenant husband's holy protectiveness, love that will not share the heart it redeemed.

note_body: God promises kings to a man still waiting on the son of promise, and Matthew's genealogy quietly keeps the receipts — David the king rising out of Abraham's line on the way to Jesus. Heaven's arithmetic outlasts today's evidence.
lens_gloss: to bear fruit, flourish — Eden's blessing verb spoken over an aged and waiting man; fruitfulness begins as God's doing, not ours.

note_body: The report counts four hundred men, but Proverbs counts differently: when a man's ways please the LORD, even enemies are turned toward peace. Morning would prove it with an embrace instead of a battle.
lens_gloss: brother — the report says 'thy brother Esau' before it counts four hundred men; kinship is named ahead of the threat.

note_body: Twelve wells and seventy palms by the water look ahead to the city where the tree of life yields twelve harvests beside the river. God has always ended hard roads at shade and water, and He always will.
lens_gloss: to pitch camp, rest — provision includes permission to stop; God's mercy furnishes the resting place, not only the road.

note_title: The laughter God read as faith.
note_body: Genesis shows the facedown laughter and the impossible arithmetic; Romans insists Abraham was not weak in faith even so. God knows the difference between mockery and a hope too large to hold quietly.
lens_gloss: to laugh — honest, facedown, overwhelmed; the root God will plant in Isaac's name rather than hold against his father.

note_title: Seventy souls, a sky of stars.
note_body: Moses does the math of mercy — seventy went down to Egypt and a night sky came out. Hebrews traces the sum back further still: from one man as good as dead, a family no one can number.
lens_gloss: star — seventy travelers became a night sky; God measures increase by His promise, never by the size of the beginning.

note_body: Generations later Peter stands in Jerusalem quoting this very sentence to a listening crowd: ye are the children of the covenant. The blessing that left Moriah is still arriving at doorsteps, including yours.
lens_gloss: seed — one small word holding a family, a nation, and the one Descendant through whom every nation is blessed.

note_body: Jacob sends word ahead while the road still lies between the brothers, and Jesus counsels the same urgency — agree with thine adversary quickly, whiles thou art in the way. Peace loves an early messenger.
lens_gloss: messenger, angel — the same word for the angels who just met Jacob; he answers heaven's messengers by sending his own toward peace.

note_title: A song and a psalm agree.
note_body: What Israel saw once at the sea, the psalmist calls God's everyday manner — He still gathers deep waters into a heap and lays them up in storehouses. The power that parted your impossible is not a one-time wonder; it is His ordinary rule.
lens_gloss: breath, wind, Spirit — the same breath that heaps the sea moves without hurry; God's power never pants or panics.

note_title: A deathbed charge, an apostle's word.
note_body: Jacob's sons carry out their father's instruction without fanfare, and Paul names the quiet principle underneath: children obeying "in the Lord: for this is right." Faithfulness rarely looks dramatic — it looks like doing the next thing you were asked.
lens_gloss: to command, to charge — a father's charge becomes the sons' quiet doing; love keeps its word one instructed step at a time.

note_body: Romans lifts the very sentence God spoke under the stars — "So shall thy seed be" — and shows Abram believing against hope. The picture God gave one worried man became the pattern for everyone who hopes past what the room can prove.
lens_gloss: seed, offspring — one small word stretched to hold a sky of stars; God's promise always outgrows the eye that first receives it.

note_body: Naomi counts her closed doors the way Abraham once counted his hundred years — honestly, and out loud. God heard the impossible arithmetic in both houses and answered it with a child neither could have produced.
lens_gloss: hope — literally a cord to hold; Naomi believes the rope has run out, but God still grips the other end.

note_title: A dying man's word, called faith.
note_body: What Joseph whispers at the edge of life, Hebrews names among faith's great acts: he made mention of a departure he would never march in. Hope with a backbone trusts God's visit beyond its own availability.
lens_gloss: to visit, attend to, look after — doubled here, "visiting He will visit"; God's coming care is stated beyond all question.

note_body: The word the Lord proclaims to Moses — longsuffering — is the very word Peter reaches for when believers fear that delay means neglect. What looks slow, both testaments say, is patience making room for mercy.
lens_gloss: steadfast, covenant-keeping love — mercy with a grip; the goodness proclaimed here is loyalty that refuses to let go across generations.

note_body: The covenant roll God reads to Abram — Hittites, Amorites, Jebusites and the rest — reappears when His Angel goes before Israel into the land; the list becomes a marching order. God does not speak in mist; He keeps track of every name He promised.
lens_gloss: "the ancient one," from qedem, the old east — even a name in God's list roots the promise in real ground and long history.

note_title: The Son shows what right looks like.
note_body: Moses calls Israel to do the right and the good in God's sight; Jesus lives it, saying He always does what pleases the Father — and is never left alone. Obedience is not a performance for approval but a beloved child walking close.
lens_gloss: straight, upright — a road that runs true; the right thing is simply the path with no crookedness in God's sight.

note_body: Jacob puts space between his droves; Isaiah says the farmer's careful sequence of plowing and sowing was taught to him by God Himself. Discretion — knowing what goes first and what can wait — is holy instruction, not mere strategy.
lens_gloss: space, breathing room, relief — Jacob builds margin between the droves; sometimes the space you leave is itself an act of trust.

note_title: First the blade, then the ear.
note_body: Genesis plants continuation inside creation — seed within the fruit — and Jesus points to the same earth bringing forth "first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn." God's promises grow in stages, and the small green beginning is already the harvest speaking.
lens_gloss: fruit — each piece carrying tomorrow's seed inside it; God builds continuation into every blessing He plants.

note_body: Stephen quotes this very verse with the doubling intact — "I have seen, I have seen" — because God's sight of suffering was worth saying twice in both testaments. The God who watched Egypt closely came down to deliver, and He has not lost that habit.
lens_gloss: to see — doubled in Hebrew, "seeing I have seen"; God's sight of your affliction is emphatic, sustained, and never casual.

note_title: As it is written, still true.
note_body: Paul takes God's "As for me" to Abram and sets it before the God "who calleth those things which be not as though they were." The covenant did not wait on Abram's ability, and your future does not rest on yours.
lens_gloss: covenant — a bond God binds Himself to keep; the future rests on His oath before Abram contributes a single thing.

note_title: Good news from a far country.
note_body: The word about Nahor's family reads like a footnote, but Proverbs knows what such news is — cold water to a thirsty soul. Hidden in that quiet report is Rebekah's family line, the next chapter of promise arriving as ordinary mail.
lens_gloss: to tell, make known, set before — heaven's next chapter often arrives as plain human news, carried by ordinary voices.

note_title: None else, and idols are nothing.
note_body: Moses presses the truth into the heart — the Lord is God, there is none else — and Paul draws the conclusion for a city full of idols: an idol is nothing in the world. Whatever has felt too large in your heart lately belongs on that same list of nothings.
lens_gloss: to know — settled, lived-in knowing, not a passing nod; truth pressed into the heart until it steadies the whole house.

note_body: Joseph falls on Benjamin's neck and weeps, and Jesus paints the Father running to fall on the prodigal's neck the same way. Restored love in Scripture is not a concept; it has arms, and it holds on.
lens_gloss: to weep aloud — restored love in Scripture is audible; tenderness is allowed to be heard, not merely explained.

note_body: Moses sang that the peoples would hear and be afraid, and forty years later Rahab confirms it almost word for word from inside Jericho's wall. The reactions swirling around God's people never once altered where He was taking them.
lens_gloss: to tremble, be shaken — the nations quake at the edges of God's acts; His children need not be steered by the tremors.

note_body: The angel's verdict — "thou hast not withheld thy son" — becomes heaven's own testimony in Paul: God "spared not his own Son." The Father never asks a surrender He was unwilling to make Himself, and His giving ends with "all things."
lens_gloss: to withhold, hold back — Abraham held nothing back, and heaven answered in kind with a Son who was not spared.

note_body: Generations after Joseph binds Israel with his oath, Moses walks out of Egypt carrying those very bones and repeating the very words: "God will surely visit you." A promise remembered is a promise that travels.
lens_gloss: to swear, bind by oath — Joseph turns hope into a promise others must carry; remembrance is built into the future on purpose.

note_title: Marah's question, answered on a hillside.
note_body: Israel murmurs, "What shall we drink?" and centuries later Jesus takes up the exact question — what ye shall eat, what ye shall drink — and answers it with a Father who already knows. The need was never the sin; the forgetting was.
lens_gloss: to murmur, grumble — need that stopped speaking to God and started speaking about Him; patience invites the question back into prayer.

note_title: Even the sun knows its setting.
note_body: The fourth day closes the way God designed days to close, and the psalmist marvels at the very lights made that day: "the sun knoweth his going down." If creation keeps God's closing rhythm without anxiety, your day is allowed to close too.
lens_gloss: evening — in God's reckoning the day begins at evening; rest opens the day, and closing well is part of the design.

note_body: God tells Abram the return will take generations, and Peter explains the clock: a day and a thousand years sit the same in God's hands. What feels like lateness to us is precision — mercy and justice arriving exactly full.
lens_gloss: full, complete, whole — the root of shalom; God's justice never arrives early, and His patience is measured, not absent.

note_body: Moses joins loving God with walking in His ways, and Jesus closes the circle: the one who keeps His commandments is the one who loves Him — and is loved by the Father in return. Obedience was never the opposite of affection; it is affection in motion.
lens_gloss: love — the command opens with it; obedience here is love walking in God's ways, not fear performing for approval.

note_body: God speaks an expanse into the middle of the waters, and Jeremiah names what was working: power made the earth, but understanding stretched out the heavens. The room God makes inside your overwhelm is not luck — it is His wisdom, on purpose.
lens_gloss: expanse, something hammered out wide — God spreads breathing room through the middle of the flood, not only after it.

note_title: The wind still knows His voice.
note_body: At the sea Moses sings that God blew and the waters obeyed; in a fishing boat the disciples marvel that "even the winds and the sea obey him." The authority that ended Egypt's pursuit has not changed hands.
lens_gloss: to sink straight down — the pursuing threat drops like lead the moment God's timing arrives; deliverance is never rushed, never late.

note_body: Before Jacob faces Esau, he prays back what God already said — "thou saidst... I will deal well with thee" — and Paul turns that instinct into a command: in every thing, let your requests be made known. Fear brought into prayer stops steering the heart.
lens_gloss: to do good, deal well — God's stated intention toward Jacob; fear is answered by praying His own words back to Him.

note_body: Joseph tells his brothers "it was not you that sent me hither, but God," and Jesus uses the same reversal with His disciples: "Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you." When God's sending is the deepest fact of your story, harm can be named without getting the last word.
lens_gloss: to send — commissioned, not merely carried along; Joseph reads his painful road as a sending with purpose at the end.

note_body: The law says none shall appear before the Lord empty, and David refuses the shortcut centuries later: he will not offer what costs him nothing. Redeemed life gives from gratitude, not from fear's tight fist.
lens_gloss: to redeem, buy back at a price — life is not self-owned but reclaimed; love pays to bring back what belongs to God.

note_body: God names the heavens and sets the evening-and-morning rhythm over creation; in the tabernacle, Aaron tends the lamp "from evening to morning" by that same beat. Worship learned creation's rhythm — and your pressured days can too.
lens_gloss: to call, to name — God names what stretches over you before you ever stand beneath it; His word defines the day.

note_title: Grief loud enough to name a place.
note_body: The Canaanites named a threshing floor after Egypt's weeping, and David turned his sorrow for Saul and Jonathan into a lament a whole nation could learn. Mourning that is allowed to be witnessed becomes a landmark others can find.
lens_gloss: mourning — grief so weighty it renamed the ground itself; sorrow given public form instead of being managed into silence.

note_title: A touched hip, a given thorn.
note_body: Jacob's strongest muscle is put out of joint by a touch, and Paul's soaring revelations come with a thorn to keep him low. Both men carry the mark so that grace, not stamina, is what holds them up.
lens_gloss: to touch — a single gentle contact, not a blow; God ends the wrestling with a touch, reaching what endurance alone could never heal.

note_body: Joseph kisses a face he had long since been reconciled to, and Jesus weeps at a tomb He is about to open. Neither restoration nor resurrection asks love to skip its tears.
lens_gloss: to weep aloud — Scripture's ordinary word for tears, given without shame to patriarch and Savior alike.

note_body: Moses prays 'that I may know thee,' and Jesus calls that very knowing life eternal. What the servant begged for on the mountain, the Son declares is the whole point of salvation.
lens_gloss: to know — not information but intimate acquaintance; Moses asks for God Himself, not merely a map through the struggle.

note_title: A purchased cave, a kept story.
note_body: Jacob's sons lay him in the cave Abraham bought, and centuries later Stephen is still recounting how the fathers were laid to rest in ground purchased in faith. Grief placed in God's keeping does not vanish — it becomes testimony the generations can stand on.
lens_gloss: to bury — grief laid down in a bought and promised place; sorrow entrusted to covenant ground instead of endless analysis.

note_body: Moses tells Israel that hearing and obeying leads to it being well with them, and Paul hands children in Ephesus the very same words — 'that it may be well with thee.' The blessing God wraps around obedience has not aged a day between the testaments.
lens_gloss: to hear — in Hebrew, listening and obeying live in one word; the beloved hear with feet ready to move.

note_title: The God who calls futures forth.
note_body: Over Ishmael, God speaks blessing where Abraham saw only a complication; in Romans, He calls things which are not as though they were. The Father's mercy writes a future for people we had quietly filed under disappointment.
lens_gloss: to bless — God's own mouth endowing good; His favor rests even on the son outside the expected line.

note_body: Joseph sets healers to honor his father's body, and Nicodemus brings a hundred pounds of myrrh and aloes for his Lord's. Some love shows itself in careful, unapplauded service to what remains.
lens_gloss: to heal — the 'physicians' here are literally 'the healers'; even when healing is past, love still tends what remains.

note_body: The sun breaks over Jacob just as his new limp begins, and Malachi promises that same rising — the Sun of righteousness with healing in His wings. Morning does not erase the mark; it shines on the one who carries it.
lens_gloss: to rise, break forth as light — the very verb Malachi uses when the Sun of righteousness rises with healing in His wings.

note_body: From a burning bush God says 'Moses, Moses'; from a blinding light, 'Saul, Saul.' When the Lord doubles your name, He is not making an announcement — He is beginning a relationship that will redirect your whole life.
lens_gloss: 'behold me' — the servant's whole-self answer to being called by name; unhurried attention become availability.

note_body: Abram walks ground God promised while the Canaanite still holds it, and Hebrews says he lived there like a stranger, dwelling in tents. Faith keeps walking difficult terrain because the promise, not the ease, is the proof of ownership.
lens_gloss: to pass through, cross over — the pilgrim's verb; Abram traverses promised ground he does not yet possess.

note_body: Boaz settles the matter before the elders where every word can be weighed, and Paul urges the same — honest things in the sight of the Lord and of men. Love that takes responsibility is never afraid of witnesses.
lens_gloss: to redeem as next of kin — to buy back what belongs to family; duty and love spoken plainly before witnesses.

note_body: Joseph's brothers invent a punishment he never planned, running from a grudge he does not hold. Proverbs names the ailment: guilt flees where no pursuer is — while grace stands still, waiting to be believed.
lens_gloss: to bear a grudge, nurse hostility — the fear that forgiveness was only politeness with an expiration date.

note_title: The road that became a creed.
note_body: Isaac sends Jacob toward Syria and Laban's tents, and generations later Israel recites it at the altar: 'A Syrian ready to perish was my father.' The detour you did not plan may become the testimony your children memorize.
lens_gloss: to send — a son dispatched onto an unplanned road that God quietly folds into covenant history.

note_body: At Sinai Moses names the people's stiffness and begs God to come near anyway; at Kadesh he prays it again — pardon according to the greatness of Thy mercy. Honest intercession never pretends the people are easy; it simply refuses to let go of the Lord.
lens_gloss: to pardon — a verb Scripture uses of God alone; the forgiveness only He can give to a stiff-necked people He still claims.

note_body: Joseph keeps seven days of mourning at the threshing floor, and Job's friends sit seven days in the dust saying nothing, because they saw his grief was great. Some sorrow does not need commentary — it needs company and a calendar that is not in a hurry.
lens_gloss: to lament aloud — chest-beating grief given voice and time; sorrow allowed to breathe instead of being rushed.

note_title: The Spirit still broods over deeps.
note_body: Genesis shows the Spirit hovering over dark, unformed waters, and the psalmist answers that when God sends that same Spirit, things are created and the face of the earth is renewed. What is formless in you is not abandoned — it is being brooded over.
lens_gloss: to hover, flutter — the word for a mother bird brooding over her young; the Spirit broods over what is not yet formed.

note_body: The psalmist says those sheltered in God can shout for joy even while danger is real, and Paul explains why: for those who love Him, all of it is being worked toward good. Rejoicing is not denial — it is what refuge sounds like.
lens_gloss: to take refuge — not mere belief but running under cover; the joy of the sheltered, not the exposed.

note_body: Israel says, 'Joseph my son is yet alive: I will go,' and the father in Jesus' parable says, 'this my son was dead, and is alive again.' Across the testaments, revived hope speaks the same sentence — my child lives, and love is already moving.
lens_gloss: alive, living — the small word that raises an old man's buried hope back onto its feet.

note_body: Joseph buries his father and then returns to Egypt, to duties that did not pause for his grief; the delivered man of Gadara is sent home to tell what compassion has done. The sacred journey ends where mercy gets practical — at your own front door.
lens_gloss: to return, turn back — the road home after holy ground; faithfulness resumed in ordinary places.

note_body: Genesis closes the fifth day with its calm refrain — evening, morning, done — and Paul promises the same Maker will carry His good work in you through to completion. The God who is never frantic will not leave you half-made.
lens_gloss: evening — Scripture counts each day from dusk: it begins in the dark and moves toward light, on God's unhurried clock.

note_title: A tent then, an open door now.
note_body: In Moses' day, whoever sought the Lord walked out to a tent beyond the camp; Jesus promises every seeker still finds, and every knock meets an opened door. The address has changed — the welcome has not.
lens_gloss: to seek, search after — the deliberate walk out to the place where God may be found.

note_title: The way out was already caught.
note_body: Abraham lifts his eyes and finds the ram God had already placed, and Paul promises that with every trial God makes a way of escape. Fear insists there is one narrow ending — faith looks again and finds provision waiting in the thicket.
lens_gloss: to see — the root beneath Jehovah-jireh: what God sees, God provides; lifted eyes find the answer already caught.

note_title: Weeping the whole house could hear.
note_body: Joseph gives his voice to his tears until Pharaoh's household hears them, and at Miletus the elders weep aloud on Paul's neck without one word of apology. In both rooms love is audible — and nobody calls it failure.
lens_gloss: voice, sound — Joseph literally 'gave his voice' to weeping; emotion allowed to be heard, not edited into silence.

note_body: Egypt gives Jacob seventy days and Israel gives Moses thirty; in both, sorrow is granted a full calendar rather than a hurried exit. Hope that is truly eternal can afford to let weeping take its time.
lens_gloss: to be full, fulfilled — the mourning days are 'filled up'; grief granted its complete number, nothing shortchanged.

note_body: Israel leaves Egypt and lands not in aimlessness but at Sinai, where covenant waits; Stephen sums it up — God brought them out and kept working wonders through forty wilderness years. The Deliverer does not drop His people at the border of freedom; He walks the middle miles too.
lens_gloss: wilderness — not wasteland but meeting ground; the in-between place where God gives His people covenant belonging.

note_body: Joseph loads his brothers with grace and still says, do not quarrel on the way; Paul tells the church to put away bitterness, wrath, and clamour. Mercy gives you the road home — refusing the old argument is how you keep it.
lens_gloss: to be agitated, tremble with anger — Joseph's charge: do not let old tremors shake a road grace has just opened.

note_title: He names them, then outlasts them.
note_body: In covenant God reads out the full roster of nations standing on Abram's promise, and in Deuteronomy the same names return — seven nations greater and mightier — on the day they are finally displaced. God is not vague about your obstacles; He numbers them, and then He outlasts them.
lens_gloss: the Amorite — the land's strongest occupant, named inside the covenant itself; God lists every obstacle He intends to outlast.

note_title: A blessing spoken over the unseen.
note_body: Isaac blesses Jacob with a multitude the fleeing young man cannot yet see, and Paul names the God who makes such speech safe — the One who calls things that are not as though they were.
lens_gloss: God Almighty — the name invoked when the promise is far bigger than the person receiving it.

note_title: A burning bush and a temple courtyard.
note_body: The name given to Moses at the bush is the very name Jesus takes on His own lips — before Abraham was, I am. The presence that steadied a shepherd in the wilderness now stands in the flesh, still unshaken.
lens_gloss: "I am" or "I will be" — the ever-present One whose being does not fluctuate with any unstable circumstance.

note_title: The commission, sung back as praise.
note_body: What God spoke over humankind at creation, the psalmist sings back to Him in wonder — dominion over the works of His hands. The responsibility that could feel like weight becomes worship when it is remembered as gift.
lens_gloss: To bless — God speaks good over His children before He assigns them anything, so the calling rests inside the blessing.

note_body: Abraham says "we will come again" while walking toward the hardest altar of his life, and Hebrews tells us what that plural was carrying: he reckoned God able to raise the dead. Worship under pressure can still speak of return.
lens_gloss: To bow down, to worship — bending the whole body low before God even while the heart carries unresolved weight.

note_body: When Jesus is asked for the greatest commandment, He reaches back to Moses' list and lifts out its beating center — love the Lord with all your heart and soul. The requirement was always an invitation into love.
lens_gloss: To love — covenant love that binds heart, soul, and daily walk together; the whole list flows out of this one word.

note_title: Seed to harvest, Eden to parable.
note_body: The earth that answered God's word at creation is still answering in Jesus' parable — first the blade, then the ear, then the full corn. Fruit rises quietly, each after its own kind, without checking the field next door.
lens_gloss: Kind, species — each living thing bears fruit true to what God made it, not to its neighbor's pattern.

note_title: The second call became an oath.
note_body: Hebrews looks back at that second calling from heaven and hears God swearing by Himself, since He could swear by no greater. The voice that returned after the knife was lowered was securing a promise that still holds us.
lens_gloss: To call out, to summon — the voice of God that keeps reaching for a person even after the crisis has passed.

note_title: The pause where the voice waited.
note_body: Stephen notices the order of that morning: only as Moses drew near to wonder did the voice of the Lord come to him. The turning aside was not a delay in his calling — it was the doorway into it.
lens_gloss: To turn aside from one's path — the small detour of honest attention where holy encounter begins.

note_title: The ground still answers His voice.
note_body: Isaiah names the God who spread out the earth and what comes from it as the same God who gives breath and spirit to the people walking on it. The word that called life from soil still sends living people back into real ground.
lens_gloss: Living creature, breathing life — the embodied, particular life God's word summons out of actual ground.

note_title: The road and the resting place.
note_body: Jacob walks a hard road toward Haran, and the psalm answers him step for step: God compasses the path and the lying down. The very night Jacob lies down on that road, heaven opens over him.
lens_gloss: To go out, to depart — the leaving that faith requires before the destination can be understood.

note_title: The gospel, preached to Abram first.
note_body: Paul calls Genesis 12:3 the gospel preached beforehand — the promise that widened one man's blessing to every family on earth was already carrying Christ toward the nations. A blessed heart was never meant to live in defense.
lens_gloss: Family, clan — the blessing aims at whole households of the earth, refusing to stop with one blessed man.

note_body: Isaiah lifts Moses' shoreline verse almost word for word and points it at a deliverance still to come — the Lord my strength and my song. Borrowed strength is a song every generation gets to sing for itself.
lens_gloss: Strength, might — not mustered from within but received, the Lord Himself becoming the singer's strength.

note_body: Paul hears Genesis 17 come to fullness in the Jerusalem above, "the mother of us all." The blessing spoken over one aging woman became a family line wide enough to include nations she would never meet — including us.
lens_gloss: Nations, peoples — one blessed life widening outward into whole nations, far beyond what the receiver could imagine.

note_title: Set in the sky, set among nations.
note_body: The God who set lights in the heavens says to His servants, "I have set thee to be a light." In both testaments the shining starts with being placed, not with promoting ourselves into view.
lens_gloss: To give, to set, to place — the lights shine where God puts them; placement, not self-promotion, makes them useful.

note_title: Loved, blessed, and shown His face.
note_body: Deuteronomy lists covenant blessings of womb, land, and flock; Jesus names the deepest one — to those who keep His word, the Father's love arrives as His own manifest presence. That is a blessing no barren season can cancel.
lens_gloss: Fruit — the produce of womb and land, and by extension every quiet form of life God keeps alive in you.

note_body: The doves Abram gathered for covenant reappear in Mary and Joseph's arms at the temple, the offering of the poor carried in with the Promise Himself. Small, concrete obedience is how God's biggest promises get prepared.
lens_gloss: To take, to fetch — obedience begins by taking in hand the concrete things God names, one step before the map.

note_body: In Egypt every brother received clothing from the very one they had wronged; in Revelation, white robes are given to every one. Grace does not ration its covering, even where the portions differ.
lens_gloss: A change of garments — the old covering exchanged for new, shame traded for dignity by the giver's hand.

note_title: A timbrel and a throne room.
note_body: Miriam's call to sing because the Lord has already triumphed finds its final chorus in the multitude crying "Salvation to our God." Worship on the far shore has always started with what He finished, not what we must prove.
lens_gloss: To sing — praise that answers God's completed act before any new striving begins.

note_title: Separated, because they are not the same.
note_body: God divides light from darkness at the very start, and Ecclesiastes draws on that first division: wisdom excels folly as far as light excels darkness. What the Father separated, the heart should not seat side by side.
lens_gloss: Light — the first thing God saw and called good, evaluated and set apart before any human eye could judge it.

note_title: A tent, an altar, a promise.
note_body: Hebrews says Abraham lived in tents because he was still waiting on promise — and Genesis shows what he raised beside them: an altar. Worship never waited for his circumstances to settle.
lens_gloss: Altar — a built place of meeting God, raised even beside a tent that may move tomorrow.

note_title: The name withheld, the blessing given.
note_body: Jacob asks for a name and receives a blessing instead, and Revelation shows the risen Christ still carrying a name no man knows but He Himself. Some of who God is stays mystery — yet His blessing arrives anyway, right there.
lens_gloss: Name — the identity Jacob demanded to grasp; God withheld the explanation but not the blessing.

note_title: Wherever the name is, He comes.
note_body: The promise of the earthen altar — "where I record my name I will come unto thee" — becomes Jesus' promise to any two or three gathered in His name. Presence never required a grand building, only His name honored.
lens_gloss: To remember, to cause a name to be honored — wherever God sets the memory of His name, He promises to come near and bless.

note_body: Jacob's vow of a tenth echoes what Hebrews remembers of Abraham before Melchizedek: the blessing came first, and the tenth followed. In both stories devotion answers grace — it never bargains for it.
lens_gloss: To give a tenth, to tithe — Jacob's doubled vow of returning a portion, gratitude responding to grace rather than purchasing it.

note_body: The order of the fifth day still holds in the psalm: He blesses them "so that they are multiplied greatly." Increase follows blessing, and a heart being restored gets to breathe under that same order.
lens_gloss: To be fruitful — increase that flows out of spoken blessing, not out of anxious effort.

note_title: The promise kept, the cities standing.
note_body: What Moses foretold on the plains, Joshua confirms inside the land — cities they never built, vineyards they never planted, and them dwelling in it all. Inherited grace makes gratitude, not entitlement, the honest response.
lens_gloss: To swear an oath — God's sworn word to the fathers, the foundation under every gift His children did not build.

note_title: Promised to Abram, released through Christ.
note_body: Paul traces the line straight through: the blessing spoken over Abram before he saw any proof reached the nations through Jesus Christ. Trust that obeys before it sees becomes a channel wider than one lifetime.
lens_gloss: Blessing — not only something Abram receives but something he becomes, good flowing through him to others.

note_body: Proverbs names what Genesis quietly shows: the king's heart turns like watercourses in the Lord's hand. So when Pharaoh says "go up," Joseph is not forcing a door — he is walking through one God already opened.
lens_gloss: To go up — the released, unforced ascent; permission granted so obedience can simply walk, without scheming.

note_body: Miriam leads the women out with timbrels after the sea; centuries later Anna the prophetess stands in the temple giving thanks over redemption come in person. Deliverance keeps turning into testimony that others can join.
lens_gloss: Prophetess — a woman carrying God's word into public praise, leading others from private relief into shared worship.

note_title: Sold by brothers, sent by God.
note_body: Joseph told his stunned brothers that God had sent him ahead of them, and centuries later Stephen stood before the council and told it the same way: they sold him, but God was with him. Two tellings, one truth — the wrong was real, and the Presence that rode into Egypt with that boy was realer still.
lens_gloss: preservation of life, sustenance — from chayah, to live; the whole aim of God's strange sending was to keep His people alive.

note_title: Prevailing looked a lot like weeping.
note_body: Genesis gives us Jacob's grip; Hosea leans in close and tells us what that grip was made of — he wept, and made supplication. The hold that would not let go was never muscle at all, but a humble, hungry asking, and that is how hope wins its blessing.
lens_gloss: to bless — kin to berek, the knee; blessing meets the one who bows low and still will not let go.
